The key claim is that task-conditioned persona selection — choosing *who* is in the group based on task characteristics — is more important than the coordination mechanism or the size of the panel. Evaluated on US stocks over an out-of-sample period, FinPanel outperforms fixed-panel configurations of equal size, prior LLM-based trading agents, and rule-based and reinforcement-learning baselines, while also exhibiting shallower drawdowns than a buy-and-hold strategy and maintaining performance without any warm-up history. The findings suggest that group composition should be treated as a per-task design decision made prior to determining how agents coordinate.
items.citation: Boming Yang, Yuquan Wang, Jiaxian Guo et al.. Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
items.summary: This paper introduces STAMP, a generative design framework for formed sheet metal panels that embeds manufacturing constraints directly into the shape representation rather than enforcing them through penalty terms during optimization. Each panel is described by a material layout and a depth map defining a single height per planar position, which inherently prevents undercuts and fixes nominal thickness, ensuring every generated or optimized panel is manufacturable by construction. The system uses boundary-conditioned diffusion to generate novel panel layouts and employs predictor gradients to optimize surface geometry while preserving outlines, openings, and fixed regions. Demonstrated on automotive hood inner panels, STAMP achieves accurate surface reconstruction and can produce varied novel layouts from very few training examples, with data efficiency improving rapidly as training set size grows. Predictor-guided selection and surface optimization yield substantial reductions in structural deformation with only modest mass increases, outperforming random design selection across all tested design families.
items.citation: Jihoon Kim, Jun Hyeok Song, Wonho Ha et al.. STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Positive Weights Do Not Certify TWFE Inference: A Design Diagnostic under Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity
items.summary: This paper investigates whether positive treatment weights in two-way fixed-effects regression—often considered a sufficient condition for valid causal inference—actually guarantee adequate inference under treatment-effect heterogeneity. The authors derive a design-based diagnostic quantity that measures the worst-case mean shift in the test statistic when local treatment-effect drift is present, showing this quantity depends entirely on the study design rather than on the data-generating process. To certify or reject the adequacy of conventional inference, they develop two regular one-sided procedures: a multiplier lower bound to detect unsafe designs and a covariance-aware noncentral chi-squared inversion to certify adequacy, establishing a numerical threshold for a given nominal size and tolerance. Applying the diagnostic to several empirical panels—including a minimum-wage study where all treated-cell weights are positive—they find that positive weights alone do not certify uniform inferential adequacy, with estimated lower bounds on the shift exceeding the safety threshold in multiple cases. The paper concludes that the diagnostic usefully separates the distinct problems of point correction, uniform exposure, and statistically warranted certification of conventional two-way fixed-effects inference.
items.citation: Stanisław M. S. Halkiewicz. Positive Weights Do Not Certify TWFE Inference: A Design Diagnostic under Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Does Increasing Government Spending on Tertiary Education Provide a Return on Investment? A Bayesian Causal Inference Analysis
items.summary: This paper examined whether government increases in public spending on tertiary education generate a positive fiscal return on investment, disentangled from general economic growth. The researchers assembled a large multi-decade cross-country panel and applied continuous-treatment Multivariate Bayesian Causal Forests to jointly model changes in four tax outcomes while controlling for starting conditions, predicted funding levels, and subsequent economic growth. They found that increasing per-student university spending shifts the tax base toward direct income and profit taxation, with effects strengthening over time as graduating cohorts enter the workforce, suggesting the fiscal response takes roughly a decade to fully materialize. When a cohort's educational costs were compared against its projected career-length tax contributions, high-income economies showed a several-fold total tax return on the initial investment. Critically, the analysis also found that expanding overall university budgets without protecting spending per student yields no measurable fiscal return, underscoring the importance of maintaining per-student funding levels rather than simply increasing aggregate expenditure.
items.citation: Andrew C. Parnell. Does Increasing Government Spending on Tertiary Education Provide a Return on Investment? A Bayesian Causal Inference Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM
items.summary: This paper addresses two related problems in wireless communications: the growing complexity of sparse vector coding schemes at higher data rates, and the susceptibility of conventional multicarrier waveforms to Doppler-induced interference and high peak-to-average power ratio in doubly selective channels. The authors propose a constant-weight sparse vector coded augmented affine frequency division multiplexing scheme that represents information through constant-weight codewords with fixed Hamming weight and large Hamming distance, keeping the sparse vector set manageable while maintaining reliability. A joint support and symbol detection algorithm is developed alongside the scheme to recover transmitted information by solving sparse recovery problems. Simulations comparing the proposed approach against conventional and enhanced sparse vector coding schemes, as well as multiple channel coding options for QAM symbol protection, show reliability gains of up to fourteen decibels over existing methods. The results also reveal that the weight and minimum Hamming distance of the constant-weight codewords must be carefully balanced against modulation order and sparse recovery feasibility to optimize overall system performance.
items.citation: Zhou Lu, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Lie-liang Yang. Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM. arXiv. 2026

items.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of predicting spatially resolved gene expression profiles from routine tissue histology images, a task typically constrained by complex model architectures and small gene panels. The authors introduce GeneFlow, a framework that combines flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion, using tokenizers to encode both histological morphology and cross-gene interactions at spatial spots. Rather than predicting an intermediate velocity field, the model directly predicts gene expression while still being trained with a velocity-based flow-matching objective. GeneFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple spatial transcriptomics benchmarks, with substantial gains in large-panel gene prediction, while dramatically reducing computational cost compared to existing approaches. The authors argue that this combination of efficiency, scalability, and biological fidelity makes GeneFlow particularly suitable for clinical applications and downstream biological discovery from widely available histology images.
items.citation: Songming Zhang, Yuxiao Luo, Shifu Luo et al.. More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infection Associated With a Severe Asthma Exacerbation in a Five-Year-Old Child: A Case Report
items.citation: Yahia A, Alaoui-Inboui F, Ahmito O et al.. Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infection Associated With a Severe Asthma Exacerbation in a Five-Year-Old Child: A Case Report. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and evaluated two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR assay panels designed to simultaneously detect ten important ovine pathogens, covering both respiratory and reproductive disease agents in sheep. Each panel was designed to run across six fluorescent channels, allowing multiplexed detection within a single reaction. Validation using reference materials demonstrated excellent sensitivity, with limits of detection in the low single-digit copies per microliter range, high reproducibility with very low coefficients of variation, and strong specificity with no cross-reactivity observed between targets. Testing against a large set of clinical samples from multiple provinces confirmed strong agreement with established reference diagnostic methods. The authors conclude that these assays offer a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for differential detection and surveillance of major ovine pathogens in field settings.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics
items.summary: This review paper examines the intersection of microfluidic technologies and biosensor systems, exploring how their integration advances quantitative life sciences and molecular diagnostics. The authors survey a broad range of microfluidic approaches, including three-dimensional cell culture systems, inertial separation, acoustofluidics, dielectrophoresis, optofluidics, and immunoassays, alongside biosensor modalities such as electrochemical, electrophysiological, plasmonic, Raman, and quantum sensing. These integrated systems are assessed for their ability to detect and analyze biological targets spanning nanometer to millimeter scales, encompassing DNA, RNA, proteins, exosomes, cells, and small organisms. The review concludes that combining microfluidics with biosensing confers substantial advantages in sensitivity, speed, portability, and real-time monitoring, with meaningful implications for human and animal health diagnostics, environmental sensing, and point-of-care testing. The authors also address existing technical challenges, future development opportunities, and highlight commercially successful products that have emerged from these integrated technologies.
items.citation: Ty Downing Naquin, Chloe M. Naquin, Qian WU et al.. Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
items.summary: The paper developed a point-of-care lateral-flow biosensor designed to simultaneously detect two biomarkers—NLRC3, an inflammatory mediator, and cardiac troponin T, a myocardial injury marker—for rapid screening of acute coronary syndromes and differentiation of acute myocardial infarction from unstable angina. The biosensor employs europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel configuration, completing quantitative measurements within twenty minutes from serum samples. A Naïve Bayes machine-learning classifier was integrated to combine the two analyte readouts into a unified diagnostic decision. Clinical evaluation showed that NLRC3 alone provided moderate accuracy for identifying acute coronary syndromes but was insufficient for distinguishing between the two conditions, whereas the dual-analyte machine-learning approach substantially improved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for acute myocardial infarction versus unstable angina discrimination. The authors conclude that merging inflammatory-risk and myocardial-injury detection within a single lateral-flow platform offers a practical decentralized triage tool for acute coronary syndrome management.
items.citation: Gu X, Teng P, Li X et al.. Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Rapid carbapenemase detection in enterobacterales using a lateral flow immunoassay: diagnostic performance and association with antimicrobial treatment decisions.
items.summary: The study evaluated a lateral flow immunochromatographic assay (LFA) for rapid detection of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, comparing its diagnostic performance against commercial quantitative PCR, the Carba NP-direct test, and the modified carbapenem inactivation method, while also examining whether same-day LFA results influenced clinical treatment decisions. Both retrospective and prospective cohorts of Enterobacterales isolates were tested, with agreement metrics calculated and multivariable logistic regression used to assess the association between LFA positivity and antimicrobial treatment escalation. The LFA achieved perfect agreement with qPCR for carbapenemase detection and type identification across both cohorts, outperforming the phenotypic comparator methods, which showed notably lower sensitivity. In the prospective cohort, a majority of patients with LFA-positive isolates underwent same-day treatment escalation compared with a small minority of those with LFA-negative isolates, and LFA positivity was independently associated with treatment escalation. The findings support the LFA as a highly accurate, rapid diagnostic tool whose results are meaningfully linked to same-day clinical antimicrobial management decisions.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Genç L, Üs İZ, Tok ŞA et al.. Rapid carbapenemase detection in enterobacterales using a lateral flow immunoassay: diagnostic performance and association with antimicrobial treatment decisions.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Harnessing Plasmonic Cu2-xSe Transducers for Quantitative Near-Infrared II Photothermal Lateral Flow Exosome Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a photothermal lateral flow assay biosensor operating in the near-infrared II window for the sensitive detection of glioblastoma-derived exosomes in serum samples. The researchers constructed a photothermal probe using silica-coated copper selenide core-shell nanoparticles conjugated with anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies, exploiting the plasmonic and photothermal properties of the copper selenide component, which were characterized through both numerical simulations and experimental work. The biosensor achieved a substantially lower detection limit and broader dynamic range compared to conventional colorimetric lateral flow detection, while maintaining reliable accuracy in complex serum matrices. The study demonstrates that copper selenide nanoparticles serve as highly effective photothermal transducers, and that near-infrared II photothermal readout can overcome key sensitivity limitations that have hindered the clinical translation of lateral flow assays toward point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Liu B, Su X, Chen H et al.. Harnessing Plasmonic Cu2-xSe Transducers for Quantitative Near-Infrared II Photothermal Lateral Flow Exosome Detection.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of lateral flow immunoassay technology for detecting viral pathogens in the context of infectious disease surveillance. The authors reframe the technology not merely as a point-of-care testing tool but as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic screening and pandemic preparedness. The review systematically covers advances in signal generation using diverse nanomaterials spanning colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems, alongside multimodal and multiplex detection approaches and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation. Applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids are comprehensively surveyed, while persistent limitations including sensitivity constraints, target specificity, cost, usability, and stability are critically assessed. The authors conclude that continued development of advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection strategies could unlock the transformative potential of lateral flow immunoassay as a frontline tool for decentralized testing and global public health emergency response.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of isolating brain cell type-specific extracellular vesicles from biofluids for non-invasive monitoring of neurological conditions. The researchers combined gene expression data, proteomics, and computational analysis to identify candidate surface protein markers capable of distinguishing EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglia, while also developing a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloguing EV proteins in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays to validate their computational predictions, they confirmed that NRXN3, a transmembrane protein, is present on EVs in both cerebrospinal fluid and plasma and can serve as a neuron-specific marker. The team then successfully developed immuno-isolation methods to capture NRXN3-positive EVs, demonstrating the practical utility of their approach. Overall, the work establishes a generalizable methodology for purifying cell type-specific EVs from biofluids, with implications for studying brain diseases through minimally invasive means.
items.citation: Dmitry Ter‐Ovanesyan, Sara T. Whiteman, Tal Gilboa et al.. Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles. Nature Neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the state and trajectory of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, addressing the need for rapid, precise, and accessible testing that can function outside centralized laboratory settings. The authors survey advances in sample preparation, nucleic acid and protein biomarker detection, and imaging modalities suited to decentralized oncology contexts, illustrating their arguments with clinical case studies from diverse healthcare settings. Key enabling technologies—including microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, and smartphone-integrated devices—are critically evaluated for their translational potential alongside their current limitations. The review also analyzes funding landscapes, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the movement of these technologies from research into commercial use. The authors conclude that interdisciplinary innovation, equitable access, and integration with precision medicine will be essential for point-of-care molecular diagnostics to meaningfully advance cancer detection, therapy selection, and treatment monitoring.
items.citation: Seemesh Bhaskar, Saurabh Umrao, Hankeun Lee et al.. Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review paper examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, encompassing both the molecular mechanisms driving neurodegeneration and the therapeutic strategies being developed to address them. The authors synthesize recent advances across several domains, including the biology of apolipoprotein E, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery, alongside the complex pathological processes beyond the classical hallmarks of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. The review notes that newly approved disease-modifying therapies can slow cognitive decline by clearing amyloid plaques from the brain, though treatments capable of halting or preventing cognitive impairment altogether remain an unmet goal. The authors conclude that these collective advances are transforming both diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease, raising the prospect that the condition may eventually become not only treatable but also preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which together cause significant global morbidity and mortality. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies critical gaps in surveillance and diagnostic capacity, especially in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances discussed include molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance tools, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for improving early detection and preparedness against future hantavirus outbreaks.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring
items.summary: This mega-review examines the current state of wearable sensor technologies for continuous and non-invasive health monitoring, bringing together leading researchers to synthesize progress across the field. The authors survey chemical biosensors applied to multiple biofluids such as sweat, saliva, tears, interstitial fluid, and cerebrospinal fluid, alongside physical sensors measuring parameters like heart rate, blood pressure, and body temperature across device formats including smart contact lenses, textiles, mouthguards, wristbands, and implantable systems. The review also addresses enabling technologies including soft electronics and advanced materials, signal acquisition and transmission strategies, on-body energy harvesting, and the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning for data management and improved analytical performance. A citation network analysis is used to map the broader landscape of the field, and business, regulatory, and ethical considerations are discussed alongside the science. The authors conclude that wearable biosensors hold transformative potential for decentralized healthcare by generating unprecedented volumes of health-relevant data to support clinical decision-making, while identifying key remaining challenges and promising directions for future research.
items.citation: Laís Canniatti Brazaca, Alvaro Moreno Lozano, Beatriz Mayol et al.. Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces. 2026

items.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
items.summary: This paper studies the Vlasov–Navier–Stokes system, which couples a kinetic equation for a particle distribution function with the fluid equations governing the surrounding velocity field. The authors construct infinitely many weak solutions for smooth initial data, achieving sharpness at the endpoint of the classical Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin uniqueness scale, since uniqueness holds for velocities in the borderline space but fails just below it. The nonuniqueness is driven entirely by the fluid component via a convex integration scheme, while the kinetic equation is solved exactly; the central analytical challenge is that the particle distribution retains memory of the entire past velocity history, requiring a novel causal gluing procedure that reconstructs the system sequentially on successive time intervals. This approach produces wild solutions that are nonetheless classically strong outside a closed, exceptionally thin set of times, and a causal mollification argument extends the construction to rough, finite-energy initial data in low dimensions. Additionally, in three dimensions the authors construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality whose singular time sets have vanishing Hausdorff measure at a precise threshold.
items.citation: Xingyu Li. Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of designing optimal interpolant schedules and numerical discretizations for stochastic interpolant-based generative models, which require bridging an initial distribution to a target distribution via a probability-flow ODE. The authors introduce a framework grounded in the analyticity properties of complexified ODE trajectories, solving the joint schedule-discretization design problem exactly using conformal mapping, which yields a family of variance-preserving schedules parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing these elliptic schedules with a tailored discretization produces a new algorithm called Zoloflow, which is closely related to Zolotarev's classical optimal rational function approximants and explicitly depends on the condition number of the target distribution. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow is shown to achieve minimax optimality among oblivious score-span algorithms in terms of score query complexity, and for log-concave targets the elliptic schedule enables sampling with controlled Wasserstein error using a number of score evaluations that scales only polylogarithmically in the condition number and error tolerance. The theoretical guarantees are complemented by empirical evaluations on both synthetic benchmarks and image generation datasets, demonstrating the practical advantages of the elliptic schedule over alternative proposals.
items.citation: Cole Becker, Taylan Kargin, Kimia Hassibi et al.. Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond. arXiv. 2026

items.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
items.summary: The paper investigates whether a free lattice can contain an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices each isomorphic to the free lattice on three generators, a question posed decades ago and previously left open. The authors analyze the structure of proper self-embeddings of the free lattice on three generators, showing that any such chain would require a coherent sequence of self-embeddings with specific compatibility and fixed-point properties. Through careful case analysis of how self-embeddings interact with free generating triples and dual operations, they demonstrate that the required configuration is impossible beyond a certain length, thereby proving no such infinite ascending chain exists in any free lattice. They also establish a contrast showing that without the freeness condition, an infinite strictly ascending chain of three-generated sublattices does exist, meaning the lattice analogue of a classical chain condition for free groups fails. The entire theorem is formally verified using the Agda proof assistant under safe flags, with the proof avoiding classical principles by replacing infinite pigeonhole arguments with finite searches and induction.
items.citation: William DeMeo, Ralph Freese. No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3). arXiv. 2026

items.title: Valid Inequalities for Bilevel 0-1 Shortest-Path Problems
items.summary: This paper studies bilevel optimization problems where a leader makes binary decisions and a follower solves a shortest-path problem, aiming to characterize the valid inequalities needed to tighten the continuous relaxation of such programs. The authors employ a dualize-and-combine reformulation and demonstrate that even with ideal formulations for both the leader's decisions and the follower's primal solution set, fractional solutions can persist in the relaxation. They identify that the critical structure requiring convexification lies in the interaction between leader variables and follower dual variables, which they formalize as a leader-potential set, and they characterize valid inequalities for this set using network flow theory, introducing a family called root cuts that are sufficient to close the objective gap. Despite these structural insights, the authors prove that the associated cut generation problem is computationally hard even in very simple network settings. To address this complexity, they propose a constructive method that exploits the network structure to fix coefficients in the valid inequalities while still preserving separation guarantees.
items.citation: Bruno M. Pacheco, Margarida Carvalho, Kim Yu. Valid Inequalities for Bilevel 0-1 Shortest-Path Problems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: OpenLayout: An Open and Agentic-Driven Platform for Holistic VLSI Physical Design and Benchmarking
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of automating design space optimization in VLSI physical design, where the enormous combinatorial space of technology nodes, circuit configurations, and constraints—combined with long tool runtimes—forces heavy reliance on experienced engineers to meet power, performance, and area targets. The authors propose that large language models, enriched with distilled human design expertise, can interpret complex design contexts and reason through the optimization process in ways that conventional algorithms cannot. To realize this, they developed OpenLayout, an agentic platform employing multi-agent collaboration with embedded design knowledge to enable self-iterative design space optimization across the full physical design flow. They also introduced OpenLayout-Bench, a benchmark targeting advanced technology nodes using commercial EDA tools to systematically evaluate LLM-driven physical design automation. Experimental results show that OpenLayout achieves state-of-the-art performance with a substantial accuracy improvement over baseline methods.
items.citation: Qiufeng Li, Sizhe Tang, Quan Cheng et al.. OpenLayout: An Open and Agentic-Driven Platform for Holistic VLSI Physical Design and Benchmarking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
items.summary: This paper investigates whether photonic quantum computing based on boson sampling can be used to model complex nonlinear dynamical systems relevant to fluid dynamics. The researchers extended the existing scattershot boson sampling framework by incorporating higher photon number components — termed bright scattershot boson sampling — to overcome scaling limitations by exploiting all randomly generated input photon number distributions. Using a digital twin of the proposed architecture grounded in multiphoton statistics, they applied the scheme to two fluid-flow benchmarks: a Lorenz-type model of thermally driven convection and a model of global atmospheric circulation. The photonic approach accurately reproduced the temporal dynamics of both systems, demonstrated resilience to photon losses up to fifty percent, outperformed coherent light under comparable conditions, and exceeded the prediction horizon of a classical reservoir-computing model with equivalent query complexity. These findings suggest that near-term, noisy intermediate-scale photonic quantum devices hold practical promise for simulating real-world complex systems.
items.citation: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley et al.. Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The paper evaluated whether a rapid quantitative nucleic acid test, the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay, could serve as a primary diagnostic tool within HIV-1 testing workflows, potentially enabling both diagnosis and initial viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter. The assay was assessed for analytical range, precision, and agreement against standard-of-care methods, including comparison with four other HIV assays using plasma samples from HIV-positive and HIV-negative individuals. The assay demonstrated strong analytical performance, complete agreement with a reference quantitative assay, and a substantially faster turnaround time compared to conventional batch testing. However, positive agreement with comparator assays was imperfect, with most discrepancies occurring in samples near or below the lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. The findings underscore both the promise and the remaining limitations of deploying rapid molecular HIV diagnostics at the point of care, particularly regarding sensitivity at low viral concentrations.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Correction: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Correction: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study examined patient perspectives on point-of-care nucleic acid testing for HIV viral load monitoring as an alternative to standard laboratory tests, which can take days to return results. Participants receiving a semi-quantitative point-of-care test through a dedicated study were invited to complete acceptability surveys and in-depth interviews about their experiences with the technology. Participants generally found the point-of-care approach acceptable and preferred its faster turnaround time and the convenience of using a fingerstick blood sample collected directly in the clinic compared to conventional viral load testing. However, participants expressed a preference for an even shorter turnaround time than the approximately two hours the test required, as well as a lower limit of detection than the current threshold. The findings suggest that point-of-care nucleic acid testing could be valuable for people with HIV who are incompletely engaged in care, though improvements to speed and sensitivity would enhance its feasibility for broader implementation.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article addresses a fundamental question in exercise immunology: whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper contrasts the generally accepted view that moderate, short-duration exercise benefits immune defense with the contested claim that arduous exercise, as practiced by high-performance athletes and military personnel, suppresses immunity and raises infection risk. Opposing groups debated whether athletes are genuinely more susceptible to infection than the general population, whether exercise independently drives increased infection risk or whether confounding factors such as sleep disruption, psychological stress, travel, and nutritional deficits are responsible, and whether the biomarkers and study designs used in the field provide reliable evidence. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but could not resolve whether exercise itself is a direct causative factor in elevated infection risk among athletes. The authors conclude that the question remains open and call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from the many interrelated variables common to high-performance sport and military populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning in large language models and externalized agent-based scaffolding represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical question answering. The authors introduced a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets, applying difficulty-aware filtering and contamination screening to ensure meaningful evaluation. They tested a range of internalized reasoning models, base models, and agent-based frameworks across this benchmark. The key finding is that both approaches independently improve performance and their benefits are additive, with the best results achieved by combining an internalized reasoning model with an agent workflow. A cost-performance analysis further showed that this combination dominates other configurations, while lightweight optimization on cheaper models provides a viable path for resource-constrained deployments.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies with artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors survey a broad range of multiomics approaches — including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling — alongside deep learning methodologies capable of extracting meaningful patterns from complex biological datasets. The review analyzes how this combined framework can accelerate target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and clinical trial design. Applications across oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are examined to illustrate the practical therapeutic potential of these converging technologies. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges, including harmonization of disparate data streams, reproducibility concerns, and algorithmic bias, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence marks the beginning of a new era in bench-to-clinic medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant rates of liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. The Asia Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver convened a Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders from member countries to synthesize current evidence and respond to shifting epidemiological, socioeconomic, and technological landscapes. The taskforce developed updated clinical practice recommendations spanning thirteen major domains, including screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The guidelines aim to support healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective management decisions. Their implementation is framed as a coordinated regional effort toward reducing and ultimately eliminating the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B in the Asia Pacific.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Enhanced B cell priming induces broadly neutralizing HIV-1 apex antibodies
items.citation: Lorie Marchitto, Kshitij Wagh, Ryan S. Roark et al.. Enhanced B cell priming induces broadly neutralizing HIV-1 apex antibodies. Nature. 2026

items.title: MEmilio: a high performance Modular EpideMIcs simuLatIOn software for multi-scale and comparative simulations of infectious disease dynamics
items.summary: MEmilio is a modular, high-performance software framework designed to unify the development, execution, and comparison of diverse epidemiological models for infectious disease simulation. The framework addresses the fragmented software ecosystem in epidemic modeling by harmonizing compartmental, metapopulation, and agent-based approaches within a single architecture built on an efficient C++ core with a Python interface. Standardized representations of space, demography, and mobility allow models to be scaled across spatial resolutions and population sizes, while integration with uncertainty quantification and parameter inference tools supports applications ranging from scenario exploration to model calibration. The framework is designed to run on both personal computers and high-performance computing systems, and strict software-engineering practices including continuous integration testing are employed to ensure robustness. By unifying disparate modeling paradigms, MEmilio aims to reduce barriers to model reuse and comparison, facilitate principled examination of model assumptions, and accelerate modeling-based outbreak preparedness.
items.citation: Julia Bicker, Carlotta Gerstein, David Kerkmann et al.. MEmilio: a high performance Modular EpideMIcs simuLatIOn software for multi-scale and comparative simulations of infectious disease dynamics. Scientific Reports. 2026

items.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
items.summary: This paper investigates how the placement and penetration level of grid-forming inverters affect frequency stability in power systems transitioning away from synchronous generators. Using an exhaustive search across all possible assignments of synchronous generators and droop-controlled grid-forming inverters in the IEEE 39-bus system, the researchers evaluated frequency performance under load disturbances applied at every eligible bus. They assessed both local bus frequency metrics and aggregate frequency metrics, specifically nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency, to understand how well system-wide measures capture location-specific behavior. The results show that at a fixed inverter penetration level, placement choices alone produce substantial variation in worst-case local frequency performance. Critically, aggregate frequency assessment was found to mask the vast majority of this placement-induced variation, suggesting that relying solely on aggregate metrics could obscure whether a given inverter placement is beneficial or harmful for local frequency stability.
items.citation: Fatma Alfailkawi, Marena Trujillo, Bri-Mathias Hodge. Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: This paper theoretically investigates whether Redshift Space Distortions (RSD) could mimic parity violation signals in the galaxy four-point correlation function, a question motivated by recent observational claims of cosmological parity violation. The authors analyze the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density using Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory to third order, incorporating tidal bias, wide-angle effects through a local line-of-sight definition for each galaxy, and generalization to an arbitrary cosmological background. By expanding the four-point correlation function in spherical harmonics, they show that angular momentum selection rules encoded in Wigner symbols force all parity-odd contributions from RSD to vanish upon averaging over all line-of-sight orientations, in both the plane-parallel and wide-angle regimes. This result holds up to the leading order of general relativistic corrections and applies to isotropic estimators of the four-point correlation function. The finding is significant because it supports interpreting any detected parity violation signal as physically meaningful rather than as a systematic artefact introduced by RSD.
items.citation: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.. Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space. arXiv. 2026

items.title: EPIGRIDS: Documentation and Validation of Seven Open Synthetic Transmission Grid Cases
items.summary: This paper documents and validates a collection of seven open synthetic transmission grid test cases called EPIGRIDS, constructed using an optimization-based method rather than the graph-statistics approach underlying most existing large public synthetic grids. The cases span a wide range of scales and include geolocated substations, multiple voltage levels, and physically derived line parameters, with the larger cases accompanied by a year of hourly bus-level load data. Validation testing confirms that every case solves an alternating-current power flow from its stored operating point, and full single-outage contingency analyses complete successfully across all cases. Optimal power flow benchmarks also largely succeed, with only one base case and a small number of its operating points failing to solve in polar form. Comparison against real interconnection data reveals that the Eastern and Western cases are somewhat denser than their real-world counterparts, and graph-statistics synthetic grids built on the same geographic footprints more closely match published realism criteria, suggesting the optimization-based construction method trades some topological realism for other design objectives.
items.citation: Jonathan M. Snodgrass, Scott Greene, Thomas J. Overbye et al.. EPIGRIDS: Documentation and Validation of Seven Open Synthetic Transmission Grid Cases. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision
items.summary: This paper addresses the accurate numerical generation of particle velocities following the bi-Kappa distribution, which describes anisotropic plasma populations with suprathermal power-law tails used in kinetic simulations of space plasmas. The authors identify two key numerical problems: floating-point underflow that eliminates the largest velocity draws when the kappa parameter approaches one-half, and velocity bounds that, even when rejecting only a small fraction of draws, can substantially alter the high-energy tail of the loaded distribution. To address underflow, they evaluate a Gamma-ratio construction on a logarithmic scale, which preserves draws in both single and double precision down to very near the theoretical minimum kappa value. They demonstrate quantitatively that a velocity bound set at twenty thermal speeds can reject a seemingly negligible fraction of draws while reducing a high-percentile speed by over ten percent, cautioning against naive application of such bounds. Using chi-squared tests spanning a wide range of kappa values, including regimes where the distribution's second moments do not exist, the authors verify that their loader correctly reproduces the target distribution in terms of speed, direction, and their joint statistics out to very high percentiles.
items.citation: Keheng Zhu, Yuri A. Omelchenko. Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision. arXiv. 2026

items.title: VellSSLH: Sound Type-Guided Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of secret leakage in constant-time cryptographic programs during speculative execution, where mispredicted branches can expose secret data through observable side channels. The authors developed VellSSLH, a selective speculative load hardening tool that operates at the LLVM IR level, using programmer annotations to distinguish public from secret inputs and inferring through type analysis which values require protection during speculation. The approach inserts misspeculation-flag operations only where necessary, avoiding the overhead of blanket protection, and is accompanied by VellSCT, a checker that validates whether the resulting IR satisfies speculative constant-time security. The security guarantees are formally mechanized in Rocq by extending Vellvm's LLVM semantics with speculative execution, attacker directives, and leakage observations, with proofs that accepted programs satisfy speculative constant-time security and that a reference transformation preserves architectural behavior. Evaluation on cryptographic benchmarks shows that VellSSLH achieves meaningfully lower runtime overhead than both standard LLVM speculative load hardening and an alternative called Ultimate SLH, with particularly large improvements on certain primitives like X25519.
items.citation: Swarn Priya. VellSSLH: Sound Type-Guided Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
items.summary: The paper addresses a latency problem in large language model serving systems where agent sessions with frequent context edits invalidate cached key-value states, forcing requests to stall while re-prefill is performed before decoding can begin. The authors developed Callo, a disaggregated serving system that repurposes these invalidated KV caches as speculative drafts during the waiting period, then verifies and corrects the speculative tokens against the exact recomputed KV after prefill completes. The system improves resource efficiency by scheduling speculative work during decode-resource underutilization and preempting speculations when drafts are unlikely to be accepted. Evaluation on a two-GPU testbed using agent coding sessions across multiple model families showed modest but consistent end-to-end speedups over a standard serving baseline, with cluster-level simulations on real-world traces indicating these gains extend to larger deployments.
items.citation: Jianjun Ou, Matthew Lentz. Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integrated community-based HIV+NCD care in microfinance groups in Kenya: results from the Harambee cluster randomised trial.
items.citation: Genberg BL, Steingrimsson JA, Kafu C et al.. Integrated community-based HIV+NCD care in microfinance groups in Kenya: results from the Harambee cluster randomised trial.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era.
items.summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the rate of viral suppression and its predictors among adolescents and adults living with HIV in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era, spanning from early antiretroviral therapy initiation through two years of follow-up. Using proportional stratified random sampling and Cox proportional hazards regression, the researchers analyzed patients aged fifteen and older who initiated antiretroviral therapy at public health facilities in Shashemene City. Viral suppression was achieved by roughly seventy percent of patients, falling short of the global target, with a median time to suppression of approximately nine months. Rapid antiretroviral therapy initiation was strongly associated with earlier viral suppression, while undernutrition, poor medication adherence, and ambulatory or bedridden functional status at baseline were each independently associated with lower likelihood of achieving suppression. The authors conclude that improving timely treatment initiation, supporting adherence, and addressing nutritional status are critical strategies for closing the gap between observed outcomes and international suppression targets in this population.
items.citation: Jarso H, Asu R, Negawo S et al.. Viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.
items.summary: This study examined long-term treatment outcomes among patients with advanced HIV disease who initiated antiretroviral therapy at rural public health facilities in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, over a twelve-year period spanning multiple policy eras. Using a retrospective cohort design with routine clinical data, researchers assessed retention in care and virological outcomes at multiple time points, applying competing risk and Poisson regression models to identify factors associated with loss to follow-up and viral suppression. Retention in care was high, remaining above eighty percent at four years, and viral load suppression exceeded eighty percent among those with available test results, with outcomes improving markedly during the Universal Test and Treat era compared with earlier periods. Men and those with very low CD4 counts faced greater risk of loss to follow-up, while women and patients who initiated treatment rapidly were more likely to achieve virological suppression. The authors conclude that despite encouraging retention and suppression rates, viral load testing uptake was suboptimal and a substantial gap remained in achieving undetectable viral loads, highlighting the need for male-targeted interventions, earlier treatment initiation, and broader implementation of the World Health Organization advanced HIV disease care package.
items.citation: Kitenge MK, Fatti G, Laxmeshwar C et al.. Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.
items.summary: This study investigated why healthcare workers in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire sometimes fail to accurately record malaria rapid diagnostic test results, a problem that undermines malaria surveillance. Using a qualitative approach embedded in a broader mixed-methods evaluation, researchers photographed RDTs performed by healthcare workers and had an external panel independently interpret the results, then conducted semi-structured interviews with workers showing high versus low agreement between their recorded and independently verified readings. The key differentiator between groups was not knowledge or resource constraints but rather differing levels of confidence in negative RDT results, particularly fear that a negative test might miss true malaria in symptomatic patients. Workers with low recording accuracy more often reported deliberate falsification—changing negative results to positive or omitting antimalarial prescriptions from registers—to reconcile documentation with their clinical decisions to treat despite a negative result. The authors conclude that interventions should focus on building clinical decision-making confidence for RDT-negative fevers, expanding non-malarial diagnostic options, and creating documentation systems that allow transparent recording of non-adherence without incentivizing misreporting.
items.citation: Kouakou OMA, Bédia-Tanoh VA, Arnzen A et al.. A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.. Malaria journal. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are compromised by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and tested blood samples using the new Bioline multi-antigen RDT, conventional RDT, expert microscopy, and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and near-perfect agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity dropped notably when qPCR served as the reference standard, revealing that submicroscopic, low-density infections were frequently missed. Molecular testing detected the highest overall malaria prevalence, identifying more cases of each species and mixed infections than either microscopy or the RDT. The findings support the multi-antigen RDT for routine clinical diagnosis but underscore the need for more sensitive tools in surveillance and control efforts within endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
items.citation: Avina Vongpradith, Regina-Mae Villanueva Dominguez, Lorainne Tudor Car et al.. Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023. The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
items.summary: This paper investigated how human-driven environmental and social changes shape the geographic distribution of outbreak risk across a broad range of infectious diseases. The researchers compiled a large database of outbreak event records covering dozens of diseases and systematically evaluated multiple hypothesized drivers—including land use change, climate variables, agricultural intensification, and healthcare access—while accounting for biases in disease detection and reporting. They found that outbreak risk tends to be highest in mosaic landscapes where people and livestock coexist near forests and fragmented ecosystems, and that these factors along with long-term precipitation declines are shared drivers across several vector-borne diseases, while directly transmitted zoonoses such as Ebola and mpox share few common environmental drivers. Healthcare access emerged as a consistently important factor across diseases, with reporting rates declining substantially for each additional hour of travel time to a health facility. The authors conclude that infectious disease emergence is fundamentally multi-causal, that no universal prevention strategy is adequate, and that ecosystem-based public health interventions must be tailored to specific disease systems and paired with strengthened health infrastructure and One Health surveillance.
items.citation: Rory Gibb, Sadie J. Ryan, David M. Pigott et al.. The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases. Nature. 2026

items.title: Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance
items.summary: This paper examined the global burden of malaria caused by the two principal parasite species, focusing on how climate change, antimalarial drug resistance, insecticide resistance, and vector adaptation are reshaping transmission and control challenges. The authors conducted a systematic review of published evidence on prevalence, incidence, mortality, geographical distribution, and environmental and resistance-related determinants, drawing on major bibliographic databases alongside surveillance and modelling sources. They found substantial geographical heterogeneity in disease burden, with one species dominating in sub-Saharan Africa and the other contributing considerably elsewhere, while temperature, precipitation, and humidity were identified as key drivers of transmission suitability. Resistance to artemisinin and partner drugs, challenges in achieving radical cure for one species, and insecticide resistance combined with behavioural changes in mosquito vectors were highlighted as major emerging threats. The authors conclude that eliminating malaria will require integrated, species-specific strategies that are simultaneously sensitive to climate variability and informed by resistance patterns, underpinned by robust surveillance and resilient health systems.
items.citation: Ebrahim Abbasi. Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance. BMJ Global Health. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.citation: Hedvig Hricak, Zachary J. Ward, Fabio Ynoe Moraes et al.. Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission. The Lancet Oncology. 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the subcellular organization of proteins in the malaria parasite *Plasmodium falciparum* during its invasive erythrocytic stage, addressing the longstanding problem that a large fraction of the parasite's proteins lack known locations or functions. The researchers applied a spatial proteomics approach called hyperLOPIT, combined with supervised machine learning, to generate high-resolution protein localization maps for thousands of proteins expressed in late schizont stages. The resulting dataset resolved dozens of distinct cellular compartments, including specialized invasion-related organelles and exported sites within the host red blood cell, enabling the classification of a large proportion of previously unlocalized proteins. By integrating these localization data with comparative genomic analyses, the study also illuminated how the spatial organization of proteins reflects evolutionary pressures that have shaped *Plasmodium* biology and its adaptation to parasitic life. The work provides a comprehensive spatial proteome resource that advances understanding of parasite cell biology and the evolutionary trajectories of its organelles.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Martin Quintana Flores, Alison C. Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Evolving Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Unified Survey of Drift, Forgetting, and Adaptation
items.summary: This survey examines the challenge of deploying machine learning models in non-stationary environments where underlying data distributions change over time. The authors propose evolving machine learning as a unifying conceptual framework that integrates four interrelated challenges: data drift, concept drift, catastrophic forgetting, and skewed learning. They systematically reviewed a large body of recent literature, categorizing methods across supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning settings. A central contribution is the synthesis of these challenges into a coherent analytical perspective that highlights their structural interdependencies and the fundamental tension between stability and adaptability in continuously updating systems. The survey also reviews evaluation protocols, benchmark datasets, and real-world applications, identifying methodological limitations and open research directions for building robust, scalable adaptive learning systems.
items.citation: Ignacio Cabrera Martin, Subhaditya Mukherjee, Almas Baimagambetov et al.. Evolving Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Unified Survey of Drift, Forgetting, and Adaptation. Applied Artificial Intelligence. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper investigates the problem of associating space-based radio frequency vessel detections with Automatic Identification System trajectories to monitor maritime activity and detect vessels operating covertly. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model that uses temporal and spatial information to align individual RF detections with AIS tracks while accounting for noise and timing discrepancies. The model was evaluated on real AIS data augmented with synthetic RF detections, and its performance was benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baseline methods through bias analyses examining trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that contrasts the full matching model against a null model substantially improved both precision and dark vessel detection capability, though it retained some directional biases. Despite these improvements, the probabilistic model approaches but does not surpass a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline, suggesting that this hand-crafted single-detection formulation has not yet fully captured the complexity needed to outperform simpler heuristics.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to gravitational dynamics, going beyond simple dark energy parameterizations. The authors perform a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density and two gravitational response functions governing matter clustering and lensing, using a combination of CMB, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation, supernova, and large-scale structure datasets. They find a persistent feature in the dark energy density at intermediate redshifts corresponding to a crossing of the phantom divide, a result that is robust across different data combinations and persists when gravitational modifications are allowed. The gravitational response functions show suggestive enhancements over a similar redshift range, though these are less statistically significant, and including large-scale structure data instead favors a suppressed lensing response. The authors conclude that current deviations from the standard cosmological model are most clearly localized in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics remain plausible but require future Stage IV surveys to confirm or rule out.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigated how convolutional neural networks exploit contextual background information when classifying agricultural images, and whether the internal representations of hidden neurons can be made interpretable through a technique called Concept Induction. The researchers applied this approach across multiple agricultural datasets spanning different levels of contextual bias, examining several CNN architectures at varying network depths and patch locations within images. Quantitative image descriptors were encoded in a knowledge graph and used as background knowledge for Concept Induction, which generated logical expressions characterizing when individual neurons activate, with these expressions then statistically validated on held-out images. The study found that a substantial proportion of neuron-feature relationships were validated, with intermediate network depths showing the highest validation rates and texture-related features such as edge, Gabor, and Tamura descriptors being most frequently associated with neuron activations. Notably, stronger contextual bias in a dataset did not correspond to higher rates of interpretable neuron-feature relationships, suggesting that a network's behavioral reliance on background context and the semantic interpretability of its hidden neurons reflect distinct and separable aspects of CNN behavior.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
items.summary: This paper introduces KELP, a Lagrangian particle tracking software designed for unstructured ocean model meshes and HEALPix equal-area grids, with a particular emphasis on compatibility with coding agents driven by language models. The software computes two- and three-dimensional particle trajectories on triangular, quadrilateral, and mixed meshes, as well as on the HEALPix grid format used by kilometre-scale ocean digital twins, and includes structured documentation and task instructions that enable language models to autonomously set up, run, and process tracking experiments. Validation showed that KELP reproduced particle distributions consistent with existing trackers, and that trajectories computed on HEALPix grids converged toward those on the native model mesh as grid resolution increased, demonstrating that HEALPix output is suitable for Lagrangian ensemble statistics when original mesh data are unavailable. The agent-based workflow substantially improved the completeness of study configurations generated by multiple language models, and most experiment preparation was completed within hours. Practical scalability was demonstrated through a multi-decade Arctic ocean transport calculation and a stress test tracking an extremely large number of particles on a high-resolution HEALPix mesh.
items.citation: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin et al.. KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection systems, framing the decision for each detected bounding box as a statistical hypothesis test where the null hypothesis assumes the box contains an in-distribution object. The authors identify that the null distribution over box features varies with box size and border contact, so valid comparisons must be made only against in-distribution boxes sharing these same geometric properties, yielding distribution-free bounds on false-alarm rates. They further argue that features extracted after class-specific classification layers are suboptimal for this test, since those layers discard information about unknown objects, and instead propose reading features from the final backbone stage before class-specific processing. Based on these principles, they introduce PLUM, a training-free scoring method that pools backbone features within a box and measures their distance to in-distribution classes conditioned on matching box geometry. PLUM achieves leading out-of-distribution detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models, outperforming compared methods on both PASCAL-VOC and BDD100K datasets.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
items.summary: The paper investigates numerical instability problems that arise when computing divergences between categorical distributions that are nearly identical. Building on prior work identifying similar issues in softmax and soft cross-entropy operations, the authors demonstrate that forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler divergences, generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence, Monte Carlo KL estimates, and entropy all suffer from rounding and cancellation errors under these near-equality conditions. These instabilities affect both the forward computation and gradient calculations, with practical consequences for machine learning applications that use divergences in optimization objectives, including knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. The authors derive numerically stable reformulations for each of these operations and provide concrete implementations validated through property-based testing.
items.citation: Brandon Amos. On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over roughly a five-year period, synthesizing the scientific evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance. The review covers expanded deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostic tools, including low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, as well as digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection as a core screening and triage tool. Innovations highlighted include novel specimen types such as tongue swabs, sputum pooling for programmatic efficiency, and improved bacteriological confirmation in children through non-sputum specimens like stool and nasopharyngeal samples. Rapid molecular drug-resistance testing and targeted next-generation sequencing have also advanced, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic gains specifically in people with HIV and advanced disease. Despite these developments, significant performance, implementation, and equity gaps persist, and no biomarker yet meets WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether extracellular vesicles carrying innate immune cell-associated surface proteins could serve as blood-based biomarkers for active tuberculosis, addressing the diagnostic gap in cases where conventional pathogen detection fails. The researchers used whole-blood transcriptome profiling to identify four innate immune cell-associated surface markers, then validated an extracellular vesicle signature using bead-based immunoprecipitation before implementing it on an eight-channel microfluidic chip capable of analyzing a small plasma volume in under thirty minutes. Testing this platform in a clinical cohort demonstrated excellent discriminatory performance for distinguishing active tuberculosis from healthy controls and from other respiratory diseases, while also providing complementary diagnostic information when conventional tests yielded negative results.
