Longitudinal tracking further revealed that the signature levels declined markedly following anti-tuberculosis treatment, suggesting utility for monitoring therapeutic response. The study concludes that profiling these tuberculosis-associated immune cell extracellular vesicles represents a rapid, minimally invasive approach with strong potential for both diagnosis and treatment monitoring.
items.citation: Lee EJ, Nie C, Park S et al.. Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.. Journal of extracellular vesicles. 2026

items.title: Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.
items.summary: This review examines the persistent diagnostic challenge posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis, which disproportionately affects children and immunocompromised individuals and is complicated by low bacterial burden, diverse anatomical sites, and nonspecific clinical presentations. The authors synthesized evidence across microbiological, molecular, sequencing-based, and histopathological approaches, integrating these with an understanding of site-specific immunopathology including granuloma biology and caseous necrosis. Diagnostic tools reviewed include established molecular assays such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Ultra, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, and emerging host-response biomarkers alongside artificial intelligence-assisted histopathology, with comparative analysis spanning osteoarticular, lymph node, pleural, central nervous system, and disseminated disease. The review proposes tiered diagnostic algorithms tailored to resource-limited settings where most cases occur, and identifies gaps in current international guidance. The authors argue that aligning diagnostic modality selection with anatomical site, specimen quality, pathological subtype, and available laboratory capacity can reduce time to diagnosis and support host-directed diagnostic strategies.
items.citation: Liu Q, Jiang Y. Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Mycobacteriophages: An Integrated Platform for Rapid Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy of Tuberculosis Infection.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated an integrated platform using the lytic mycobacteriophage D29 to address the growing challenge of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis. The platform combined a rapid diagnostic module that uses multiplex real-time PCR to detect phage replication in drug-resistant bacterial isolates, thereby assessing antimycobacterial susceptibility within five days, with a liposomal therapeutic formulation designed to deliver the phage directly to the site of infection. Therapeutic efficacy was tested in a mouse model of pulmonary tuberculosis using both aerosol and intranasal delivery routes, with bacterial burden in the lungs assessed at multiple timepoints. The diagnostic component demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity across multiple anti-tuberculosis drugs, and the lyophilised components remained stable for an extended period. Both delivery routes significantly reduced bacterial burden compared to controls, with aerosol administration showing a trend toward greater efficacy, and pharmacokinetic analysis revealed exclusive lung tropism with evidence of in vivo phage replication in infected tissue and no significant toxicity or immunogenicity, supporting potential clinical translation.
items.citation: Avdeev VV, Vladimirsky MA, Eliseev PI et al.. Mycobacteriophages: An Integrated Platform for Rapid Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy of Tuberculosis Infection.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from 1990 to the present, focusing on adults living with HIV in whom tuberculosis remains the leading cause of hospitalisation and death. The authors describe the inherent diagnostic challenges in this population, including lower bacillary load in sputum, high rates of extrapulmonary and disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections. Historically, smear microscopy was the only rapid diagnostic tool available, but its reduced sensitivity in people with HIV led to both significant underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis with consequent harms. The introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside wider antiretroviral therapy use, has substantially improved diagnosis and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Nevertheless, the review concludes that no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care suitability, underscoring the continued need for novel accurate and accessible diagnostic tools.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities
items.summary: This paper investigated security vulnerabilities in large language model-based multi-agent systems, specifically focusing on how manipulated knowledge can propagate through networks of communicating agents. The researchers designed a two-stage attack methodology combining Persuasiveness Injection and Manipulated Knowledge Injection, which causes agents to spread both counterfactual and toxic information during normal communication without relying on explicit adversarial prompt attacks and without degrading the agents' general capabilities. Experiments demonstrated that these manipulations can persist through retrieval-augmented generation frameworks, where benign agents store and later retrieve corrupted conversation histories, amplifying the spread of harmful content. To counter these risks, the authors proposed two defense strategies involving system prompts that encourage critical knowledge verification and the introduction of supervisory agents to oversee agent interactions, both of which measurably reduced the rate of manipulation spread. The work concludes that LLM-based multi-agent communities harbor critical and underexplored security vulnerabilities that demand prompt adoption of targeted defenses by platform developers.
items.citation: Tianjie Ju, Yiting Wang, Yi Hua et al.. Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities. Science China Information Sciences. 2026

items.title: AI-induced never-skilling in medical education
items.citation: Yuhe Ke, Liyuan Jin, Jasmine Chiat Ling Ong et al.. AI-induced never-skilling in medical education. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach based on precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify cell-type-specific genes differentially expressed in association with traits across subjects. The tool was designed to handle complex statistical models while controlling false positive rates, and it achieves substantially faster runtimes and lower memory usage compared to existing workflows. Performance was validated on published datasets as well as a novel large-scale dataset of over a million single nuclei from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls. The work demonstrates that dreamlet enables statistically rigorous and computationally scalable differential expression analyses in large cohort-based single-cell studies of human disease.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper examined whether internalized reasoning in large language models and externalized agent-based scaffolding represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical question answering. The researchers constructed a benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets using difficulty-aware curation and contamination screening, then systematically evaluated a range of internalized reasoning models, base models, and agent-based frameworks against it. They found that both approaches independently improve performance on complex medical reasoning tasks, and crucially, that their benefits are additive rather than exclusive. The best performance was achieved by combining an internalized reasoning model with an agent workflow, while cost-performance analysis revealed this combination also dominated the efficiency frontier. The study additionally notes that lightweight optimization strategies can make these gains accessible in resource-constrained settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission

items.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes
items.summary: This review examines nanopore direct RNA sequencing as a transformative technology for studying native RNA biology and epitranscriptomics. Unlike short-read RNA sequencing or complementary DNA-based long-read approaches, the technique sequences individual RNA molecules without reverse transcription or amplification, allowing simultaneous capture of RNA modifications, full-length transcript structures, alternative splicing, and poly-adenylation tail features from single molecules. The authors trace the biophysical principles and technological evolution of the method, compare it systematically against alternative sequencing strategies, and survey optimized experimental workflows for diverse RNA types including messenger RNA, transfer RNA, circular RNA, and small non-coding species. They also review state-of-the-art computational algorithms for modification detection, isoform reconstruction, and poly-adenylation tail inference, while emphasizing the importance of benchmarking and orthogonal validation to distinguish direct signal measurements from computational predictions. The review concludes by highlighting emerging applications in resolving complex transcriptomes, characterizing coordinated epitranscriptomic regulation, identifying disease-associated RNA signatures, and outlining remaining technical challenges for deploying the technology in precision medicine and broader biological research.
items.citation: Tianyuan Zhang, Jia Li, Chao Tang et al.. Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes. iMeta. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of monitoring maritime activities by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which provides vessel identification but has known vulnerabilities, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories by jointly modeling temporal and spatial information along with noise and timing discrepancies. The approach was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines, and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full model against a null model without match transitions substantially improved both precision and the ability to detect vessels behaving covertly, while also reducing certain biases. However, a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline requiring no model fitting still outperformed the proposed Pair Hidden Markov Model, indicating that this particular single-detection formulation approaches but does not surpass simpler heuristic methods.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to gravitational dynamics, going beyond simple dark energy parameterizations. The authors perform a non-parametric joint reconstruction of the effective dark energy density and two gravitational response functions governing matter clustering and gravitational lensing, using a combination of CMB, baryon acoustic oscillation, supernova, and large-scale structure datasets. They find a persistent feature in the dark energy density around a redshift of roughly half to three-quarters, consistent with a crossing of the phantom divide, which remains robust across different data combinations and when gravitational modifications are freely varied. The gravitational response functions show suggestive enhancements over a similar redshift range, though these are less statistically significant, and including large-scale structure data instead favors a suppressed lensing response. The authors conclude that current tensions with the standard cosmological model are most clearly located in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics remain plausible but await confirmation from next-generation surveys.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigated how convolutional neural networks exploit contextual background information when classifying agricultural images, and whether a technique called Concept Induction can reveal what hidden neurons actually represent when processing such contextual patches. The researchers applied Concept Induction to five agricultural datasets varying in degree of contextual bias, analyzing multiple CNN architectures across different network depths and patch locations by encoding quantitative image descriptors in a knowledge graph to derive logical expressions characterizing neuron activations. A substantial portion of tested neuron-feature pairs were statistically validated, with validation rates being highest at intermediate network depths and driven most strongly by edge, Gabor, and texture-based features. Notably, the degree of contextual bias in a dataset did not straightforwardly predict how interpretable the hidden neuron representations were, suggesting that a network's behavioral reliance on background context and the semantic interpretability of its internal representations are distinct phenomena. The authors conclude that Concept Induction can usefully complement existing patch-based methods for detecting contextual bias by providing insight into what CNN hidden layers encode, rather than only measuring classification accuracy.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
items.summary: This paper introduces KELP, a Lagrangian particle tracking software designed to follow virtual particles through ocean model velocity fields in order to study transport pathways, connectivity, and dispersion. The tool is built to operate on unstructured ocean-model meshes as well as HEALPix equal-area grids, which are used by kilometre-scale ocean digital twins, and is specifically designed to be operated by coding agents that use language models to write and execute code. The authors demonstrate that structured documentation and short task instructions called skills substantially improved the ability of multiple language models to correctly set up and run Lagrangian studies. KELP successfully reproduced particle distributions from other established trackers, and trajectories computed on HEALPix grids converged toward those on the original model mesh as grid resolution increased, supporting the use of HEALPix output for ensemble Lagrangian statistics when the native mesh is unavailable. A multidecadal simulation tracking millions of particles in the Beaufort Gyre showed that transport to Fram Strait takes years to decades, confirming the tool's applicability to large-scale oceanographic questions.
items.citation: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin et al.. KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection systems, where a model encounters objects from classes not seen during training. The authors reframe the decision on each detected bounding box as a hypothesis test, arguing that the null distribution of in-distribution boxes varies systematically with box size and contact with image borders, so each box should be compared only against in-distribution boxes sharing the same geometric properties. This box-conditional framing provides a distribution-free bound on false-alarm rates and reveals discriminative structure that a single pooled null distribution would obscure. Building on this, the authors propose PLUM, a training-free scoring method that extracts features from the last backbone stage within a box and ranks their distance to in-distribution classes relative to geometrically matched in-distribution boxes, deliberately reading features before class-specific layers to preserve information about unknown objects. PLUM achieves state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models, outperforming compared methods on both PASCAL-VOC and BDD100K datasets.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
items.summary: The paper investigates numerical instability in standard divergence computations between categorical distributions that are nearly equal. Building on prior work identifying similar problems in softmax and soft cross-entropy operations, the authors demonstrate that forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence, generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence, Monte Carlo KL estimates, and entropy all suffer from rounding and cancellation errors under these conditions. These instabilities affect both the forward computation and gradient calculations, with practical consequences for machine learning tasks such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal optimization methods. To address these issues, the authors derive numerically stable reformulations for each operation and provide validated example implementations tested through property-based testing.
items.citation: Brandon Amos. On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.
items.venue: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
items.citation: Walia K, Gopalakrishnan R, Rupali P et al.. A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.. Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 2026

items.title: Cost and operational impact of a molecular point-of-care test for sexually transmitted infections in the emergency department.
items.summary: This study compared centralized laboratory testing with molecular point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections among female emergency department patients suspected of infection, examining both costs and operational outcomes. Using decision analysis through cost tables derived from a pre-post implementation study, researchers assessed direct testing costs, follow-up costs, overtreatment and undertreatment costs, and emergency department return visits over a twelve-month horizon from both hospital and societal perspectives. Point-of-care testing carried substantially higher direct costs than centralized laboratory testing, and this difference was not offset by savings from reduced undertreatment follow-up or societal costs associated with diagnostic errors. From a societal standpoint, point-of-care testing increased overall costs and reduced hospital revenue compared with centralized testing under current pricing and reimbursement structures. However, threshold analysis suggested that hospitals with long wait times could potentially achieve net revenue gains through improved patient throughput and more efficient use of examination room capacity.
items.venue: The American journal of emergency medicine
items.citation: Paul-Ledesma A, Dashler G, Hsieh YH et al.. Cost and operational impact of a molecular point-of-care test for sexually transmitted infections in the emergency department.. The American journal of emergency medicine. 2026

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined interventions designed to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of bacterial sexually transmitted infections—specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis—within emergency department settings in the United States. The authors searched the published literature over a multi-decade period and identified studies evaluating a range of approaches including universal screening, electronic health record prompts, point-of-care testing, and patient-directed tools. Universal screening substantially increased testing and case detection, electronic prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing improved same-day treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. Bundled interventions that addressed multiple steps in the care pathway appeared to yield the greatest overall impact, though heterogeneity among studies made direct comparisons difficult. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity, and cost-effectiveness across diverse emergency department contexts.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic in Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI/HIV point-of-care tests, and surveyed participants about demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese men, with a notable proportion of Syrian participants and a high prevalence of HIV among attendees. Despite high levels of STI and HIV awareness, condomless sex and recreational drug use were common, and perceived stigma and community beliefs emerged as significant barriers to testing. The study concludes that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day diagnosis, counselling, and linkage to care, and underscores the need to address HIV-related stigma to reduce risky behaviours in this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank
items.summary: This paper studies multi-agent interacting particle systems that feature higher-order interactions, meaning individuals can interact simultaneously in groups rather than only in pairs, with the underlying network structure represented by a hypergraph rather than a standard graph. The authors consider dense hypergraphs that are nonuniform and of unbounded rank, meaning the size of interacting groups is not fixed and can grow without bound. To derive the large-population behavior of these systems, they developed a mathematical framework combining tools from partial differential equations, stochastic analysis, kinetic theory, and graph limit theory. The central result is a rigorous derivation of a mean-field limit for this class of systems, showing that when the interaction kernels are sufficiently regular, the limiting behavior is governed by a Vlasov-type equation in which the hypergraph structure is encoded by a novel object called a UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon). This limiting equation captures interactions of infinitely many orders simultaneously, extending mean-field theory to a substantially broader class of multi-agent systems than previously treated in the literature.
items.citation: Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato. Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank. Journal of Nonlinear Science. 2026

items.title: INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials
items.summary: The paper addresses the threat posed by problematic randomised controlled trials to the integrity of evidence synthesis, where flawed or fraudulent studies can distort the conclusions of systematic reviews and clinical guidelines if left undetected. To tackle this problem, the authors developed a tool called INSPECT-SR, designed to help researchers assess the trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials by identifying concerns arising from research misconduct, fraud, or honest critical errors. The paper describes the development process of INSPECT-SR and presents both the tool itself and an accompanying guidance document intended to support its use. The intended outcome is to enable researchers to detect and exclude problematic trials from systematic reviews, thereby safeguarding the reliability of evidence-based recommendations.
items.citation: Jack Wilkinson, Calvin Heal, Ella Flemyng et al.. INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials. BMJ. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines the claim that cyberpunk fiction is the supreme literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism, subjecting it to a critical rethinking through three interrelated frameworks: cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction. The author argues that postmodernism has been deeply preoccupied with cybernetic themes while cybernetics itself has been haunted by the Gothic, and that Baudrillard's theories of simulation suggest fiction takes on a new cultural role in an era dominated by cybernetic processes. Drawing on Deleuze and Guattari's materialist reconception of the Gothic — derived from Worringer's work on barbarian art rather than conventional literary history — the thesis develops a "hypernaturalist" framework centred on the nonorganic continuum and the breakdown of boundaries between the animate and inanimate. Key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition are analysed through this lens, revealing their central concern with catatonic states, bodies that exceed their own skin, and agency without subjectivity. The thesis introduces the concept of the "flatline" — signifying both a state of unlife or undeath and a condition of radical immanence — as the convergence point where cyberpunk brings cybernetics and the Gothic together, with four chapters exploring this concept across the domains of postmodernism, the body, reproduction, and fiction itself.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
items.summary: This paper investigated the environmental and social drivers shaping the geographic distribution of outbreak risk across a broad range of emerging infectious diseases in the context of human-driven ecological change. The researchers compiled a large dataset of outbreak event records spanning dozens of diseases and systematically evaluated how multiple hypothesized drivers, including land use change, climate variables, agricultural intensification, and healthcare access, influence where outbreaks occur, while correcting for detection and reporting biases. They found that outbreak risk tends to be highest in mosaic landscapes where human populations and livestock coexist near forests and fragmented ecosystems, and that declining precipitation is a shared driver across several vector-borne diseases, whereas directly transmitted zoonoses share few common drivers. Healthcare access emerged as a consistently important factor, with outbreak reporting declining substantially for each additional hour of travel time from a health facility. The authors conclude that disease emergence is inherently multi-causal, that no universal prevention strategy is adequate, and that ecosystem-based public health interventions must be tailored to specific disease systems and paired with strengthened health infrastructure and One Health surveillance.
items.citation: Rory Gibb, Sadie J. Ryan, David M. Pigott et al.. The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases. Nature. 2026

items.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming
items.summary: This paper examined the safety and reliability of large language models used in health and medical contexts, arguing that current evaluation methods based on static benchmarks are inadequate for capturing real-world risks. The researchers developed a Dynamic, Automatic and Systematic red-teaming framework that uses adversarial agents to continuously probe models across four critical dimensions: robustness, privacy, bias, and hallucination. Applying this framework to a set of state-of-the-art language models revealed a stark "benchmarking gap," whereby models that performed well on standard medical question-answering benchmarks failed dramatically when subjected to dynamic adversarial testing. Failures were pervasive across all evaluated safety dimensions, with the vast majority of previously correct answers breaking down under robustness testing, and high failure rates also observed for privacy leakage, cognitive bias susceptibility, and hallucination. The authors conclude that strong performance on established static benchmarks likely reflects superficial memorization rather than genuine medical competence, and they propose their framework as a scalable, living audit system for identifying latent risks before clinical deployment.
items.citation: Jiazhen Pan, Bailiang Jian, Paul Hager et al.. Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing public health burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant rates of liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. The Asia Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver convened a dedicated Viral Elimination Taskforce, bringing together key opinion leaders from member countries and regions to develop updated clinical practice guidance. The taskforce incorporated evolving epidemiological trends, socioeconomic factors, and technological advances into their deliberations. The resulting guidelines provide recommendations across thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, aimed at supporting healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective decisions. The overarching goal is to reduce the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B and advance progress toward its elimination across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper investigates the challenge of monitoring maritime vessels by combining two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which provides vessel identification but has known vulnerabilities, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers applied a Pair Hidden Markov Model to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS trajectories by jointly modeling temporal and spatial information along with noise and timing discrepancies. The approach was evaluated on real AIS data paired with synthetic radio frequency detections, with performance assessed against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that contrasts the full model against a null model without match transitions substantially improved both vessel-matching precision and the detection of "dark" vessels operating without AIS transponders. Despite these improvements, the proposed model approaches but does not surpass a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline that requires no parameter fitting, suggesting that the single-detection Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation has not yet fully exploited the potential of the probabilistic framework.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to how gravity behaves, going beyond a simple dark energy equation-of-state test. The authors performed a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density alongside gravitational response functions governing matter clustering and lensing, using a combination of CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, supernova, and large-scale structure data. A persistent feature emerges in the dark energy density around intermediate redshifts, consistent with a crossing of the phantom divide, and this signal is robust across different data combinations and whether or not gravitational modifications are included. The gravitational response functions show suggestive but less significant enhancements over the same redshift range, though including large-scale structure data shifts the lensing response toward values below the standard expectation. The study concludes that current tensions with the standard cosmological model are most clearly localized in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics remain plausible but await confirmation from next-generation surveys.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigates how convolutional neural networks exploit contextual background information when classifying agricultural images, and what this behavior means for the interpretability of hidden layer representations. The researchers applied Concept Induction to hidden neuron activations on contextual image patches across five agricultural datasets, four CNN architectures, three network depths, and five patch locations, encoding quantitative image descriptors in a knowledge graph to derive logical expressions characterizing neuron behavior. These expressions were statistically validated on held-out images, with over a quarter of tested neuron-feature pairs confirmed, and validation rates were highest at intermediate network depths and for edge, Gabor, and texture features. Notably, the degree of contextual bias in a dataset did not predict how interpretable its hidden neurons were, as the moderately biased dataset yielded the highest validation rate while the most biased dataset yielded the lowest. The authors conclude that behavioral context dependence and semantic interpretability of hidden neurons reflect distinct aspects of CNN behavior, and that Concept Induction offers a valuable complement to accuracy-based methods for detecting and understanding contextual bias.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
items.summary: This paper introduces KELP v1.0, a Lagrangian particle tracking software designed to follow virtual particles through ocean model velocity fields in order to study transport pathways, connectivity, and dispersion. The tool is specifically built to operate on unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix equal-area grids, including those used by kilometre-scale digital twin ocean models, and is architected for use by coding agents — programs in which a language model writes, executes, and checks code autonomously. The authors demonstrate that structured documentation and short task instructions called "skills" substantially improved the ability of multiple language models to correctly set up and run Lagrangian studies. KELP reproduced particle distributions consistent with existing trackers, and trajectories computed on HEALPix grids converged toward those on native model meshes as grid resolution was refined, supporting the use of HEALPix output for ensemble Lagrangian statistics when the original mesh is unavailable. The software was validated through multi-decadal simulations involving tens of millions of particles, and stress-tested at exceptionally large scales, demonstrating both scientific fidelity and computational efficiency.
items.citation: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin et al.. KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection systems, where a model must identify objects belonging to unknown classes rather than only those seen during training. The authors reframe the OOD detection decision as a hypothesis test, recognizing that the null distribution of in-distribution boxes varies with box size and border contact, and that conditioning on these properties yields distribution-free false-alarm rate bounds while revealing separations that a single pooled null distribution obscures. Rather than reading class-specific layers that discard information about unknown objects, their method extracts features from the final backbone stage before class-specific processing. The resulting training-free scoring method, called PLUM, pools these backbone features within a detected box and ranks their distance to in-distribution classes against boxes sharing the same size and border contact characteristics. PLUM achieves leading detection performance on standard benchmarks without relying on external models, outperforming compared methods on both PASCAL-VOC and BDD100K datasets.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: This paper investigates whether Redshift Space Distortions (RSD) can mimic parity violation signals in the isotropic galaxy four-point correlation function (4PCF), motivated by recent observational claims of cosmological parity violation. The authors analyze the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density using Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory to third order, incorporating wide-angle effects, tidal bias, and an arbitrary cosmological background. By expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, they demonstrate that angular momentum selection rules encoded in Wigner 3-j symbols force all parity-odd contributions from RSD to vanish when averaged over all line-of-sight orientations, in both the plane-parallel and full wide-angle cases. This result holds up to the leading order of general relativistic corrections and extends previous trispectrum analyses in Fourier space. The finding is significant for large-scale structure analyses because it confirms that any observed parity-violation signal in the isotropic 4PCF cannot be attributed to RSD as a systematic artifact.
items.citation: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.. Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study investigated whether the method used to diagnose bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis influences the rate of co-detected sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic vaginitis. Researchers compared STI detection rates using nucleic acid amplification testing for four pathogens across women whose vaginal conditions had been diagnosed by clinical assessment, conventional laboratory methods, or molecular diagnostic methods. Women with a molecular diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis had significantly higher STI co-infection rates than those diagnosed by conventional laboratory or clinician-based methods, and a positive molecular vaginitis result was associated with substantially elevated relative risk for any STI. The findings indicate that an entirely molecular testing approach to vaginitis and STI diagnosis yields better STI case-finding than combining molecular STI tests with conventional or clinician-based vaginitis diagnoses. The authors conclude that unified molecular testing on a single specimen improves risk stratification, supports guideline-aligned care, and streamlines laboratory workflows.
items.citation: Getman D, Seña AC, Nenninger A et al.. Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) adherence patterns and subsequent HIV and sexually transmitted infection rates among adult men who newly initiated PrEP. Using a retrospective cohort analysis of commercially insured individuals from an administrative claims database spanning before and during the pandemic, the researchers applied group-based trajectory modeling to characterize adherence patterns and statistical modeling to compare HIV incidence and STI rates between the two groups. Those who initiated PrEP during the pandemic showed markedly worse adherence trajectories, with early discontinuation being the most common pattern, compared to a predominantly high-adherence pattern seen in the pre-pandemic group. Initiating PrEP during the pandemic was associated with a significantly higher risk of HIV acquisition, while STI rates were similar between the two periods. The findings underscore the need for targeted strategies to sustain access to and continuity of HIV prevention services during public health emergencies.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026

items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to veterinary parasitology, addressing limitations of conventional methods such as poor sensitivity, low specificity, and reliance on specialized laboratory infrastructure. The authors critically survey how CRISPR systems utilizing Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14 effectors can detect protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites with high sensitivity and speed. The review describes how these platforms are enhanced through integration with isothermal amplification techniques, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to improve field deployability. Current obstacles to wider adoption—including assay standardization, multiplex detection, regulatory approval, and commercialization pathways—are systematically discussed alongside future directions such as amplification-free assays and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics. The authors conclude that CRISPR-based diagnostics hold strong potential to advance point-of-care parasite surveillance and support One Health disease control strategies across livestock, companion animals, wildlife, and public health contexts.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of high background signal (leakage) in amplification-free CRISPR-based nucleic acid diagnostics, which limits sensitivity and precision. The researchers engineered the CRISPR/Cas12a guide RNA by adding a DNA extension to the scaffold RNA's three-prime end, creating a conformational switch that introduces steric hindrance to keep the system inhibited until a specific target is present. This redesigned guide RNA acts as a threshold-controlled molecular switch that shifts Cas12a from an inhibited to an activated state only upon target recognition, suppressing the self-activation that typically causes background accumulation in cascaded CRISPR systems. The resulting cascade system, called CALCas, achieved femtomolar sensitivity and enabled rapid detection of HPV16 and HPV18 in under thirty minutes without nucleic acid amplification. The authors conclude that this DNA-mediated allosteric regulation strategy provides a new avenue for reprogramming Cas12a enzymatic activity with stable baseline signals suitable for precise quantitative diagnostics.
items.citation: Li X, Hu H, Jiang X et al.. Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines point-of-care testing as a diagnostic strategy for infectious diseases, motivated by the growing global burden of such diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the core technical platforms underpinning current point-of-care technologies, including lateral flow assays, chemiluminescence immunoassays, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and microfluidic chip systems, as well as their application across respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, urinary tract, and sexually transmitted infections. They assessed the clinical applicability of both immunochromatographic and molecular diagnostic modalities, while also cataloguing limitations related to detection sensitivity, quality control, cost, and integration into clinical workflows. The review finds that advances in nanomaterials, microfluidic engineering, and artificial intelligence, alongside improved industry standardization, are driving enhanced performance and intelligent detection capabilities. The authors conclude that point-of-care testing holds strong promise as a core diagnostic tool for precision clinical management and public health epidemic control.
items.citation: Fang Q, Lin Y, Hu G et al.. Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how genome-wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep insights into disease mechanisms, while deep learning architectures are uniquely suited to extract meaningful patterns from these complex, high-dimensional datasets. The combined framework is shown to accelerate target identification, lead optimization, and clinical trial design across therapeutic areas including oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The review also addresses persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias. The authors argue that this technological convergence enables more precise therapeutic interventions and represents a foundational shift toward data-driven, bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance
items.summary: This paper investigated the relationship between cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of cell death mediated by ferredoxin 1 and protein lipoylation, and antitumor immune responses. The researchers found that CD8+ T cell-mediated immunity increases tumor cell susceptibility to cuproptosis, while cuproptotic tumor cells reciprocally stimulate antitumor immunity by releasing damage-associated molecular patterns that activate dendritic cells. A key mechanistic finding is that interferon-gamma produced by CD8+ T cells upregulates ferredoxin 1 expression in tumor cells through the STAT1-IRF1 signaling axis, thereby sensitizing those cells to cuproptosis. Building on this bidirectional crosstalk, the authors demonstrated across multiple preclinical models that combining a cuproptosis inducer with anti-PD-L1 therapy can overcome resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings establish cuproptosis as a form of immunogenic cell death and propose targeting this pathway as a strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in resistant tumors.
items.citation: Guang Lei, Zhengze Lu, Zhihao Xu et al.. Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance. Cell. 2026

items.title: Migration, Displacement, and Health Inequities: A Comparative Study of Refugee Populations and Access to Healthcare Services
items.summary: This paper examined healthcare inequities experienced by refugee and displaced populations across different host-country settings, with a focus on how varying levels of healthcare integration affect health outcomes. Rather than collecting empirical data, the study constructed a predictive modeling framework using published epidemiological evidence, migration theories, and humanitarian health frameworks, applying machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM to simulated data representing hypothetical refugee households distributed across four healthcare accessibility scenarios ranging from minimal to comprehensive universal access. All numerical findings are explicitly simulated and intended as a methodological template rather than as empirically derived results. The framework predicts that greater healthcare integration is associated with improved utilization, maternal and child health, chronic disease management, mental health access, and reduced inequities, with XGBoost performing best at identifying populations at risk of healthcare exclusion. The authors present this as a blueprint for future empirical research integrating migration studies, public health policy, epidemiology, and artificial intelligence to address disparities in refugee healthcare access.
items.citation: Muhammad Riaz, Neelam Tariq, Madiha Iqbal et al.. Migration, Displacement, and Health Inequities: A Comparative Study of Refugee Populations and Access to Healthcare Services. Social science review archives.. 2026

items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the emerging field of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, focusing on how decentralized testing can overcome the limitations of centralized laboratory settings to accelerate clinical decision-making. The authors comprehensively survey advances in sample preparation, nucleic acid and protein biomarker detection, and imaging modalities compatible with point-of-care deployment, illustrating their relevance through clinical case studies drawn from hospital, outpatient, and oncology practice settings. Key enabling technologies evaluated include microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, and smartphone-integrated devices, alongside a critical assessment of their limitations. The review also analyzes the funding landscape, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the translation of these technologies from academic research into commercial products. The authors conclude by projecting future directions that emphasize interdisciplinary innovation, equitable global access, and integration into precision medicine for cancer detection, therapy selection, and treatment monitoring.

items.title: Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses
items.summary: This paper investigated how hedgehog merbecoviruses — relatives of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus circulating in European and Asian hedgehogs — enter host cells. Using cell-based assays, pseudotype experiments with a vesicular stomatitis virus reporter system, and protein binding assays, the researchers identified aminopeptidase N (APN) as the cellular receptor that these viruses use for entry. Hedgehog coronavirus spike proteins showed greater infectivity when produced at temperatures matching hedgehog physiology rather than human body temperature, and a broad screen of mammalian APN orthologues revealed highly restricted cross-species receptor use, with human APN unable to support infection. Electron cryomicroscopy of the glycoprotein–receptor interface uncovered a structurally distinct binding mode compared to other known coronavirus spike–APN interactions, providing a molecular explanation for the species barrier. These findings expand knowledge of receptor utilization across merbecoviruses and betacoronaviruses while informing assessments of the zoonotic risk posed by hedgehog merbecoviruses.
items.citation: Min Jin, Victoria A. Jefferson, Zhe Zhao et al.. Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses. Nature Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Modulation of Gut Microbiota Through Functional Foods to Reduce Low-Grade Chronic Inflammation
items.summary: This paper reviewed the relationship between gut microbiota dysbiosis and chronic low-grade inflammation, which underlies conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, and cancer. The authors examined how the diverse microbial community of the gastrointestinal tract regulates immune responses, nutrient metabolism, and intestinal barrier integrity, and how disruptions to this community contribute to inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction. The review focused on dietary interventions using functional foods, particularly probiotics, prebiotics, and bioactive compounds, as strategies to restore microbial balance and suppress harmful inflammatory activity. Advances in microbiome sequencing technologies were highlighted as enabling more targeted nutritional approaches by deepening understanding of host–microbe interactions. The authors conclude that modulating gut microbiota through functional foods represents a promising and non-invasive strategy for reducing chronic inflammation and improving overall metabolic and immune health.

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper investigates the challenge of monitoring maritime vessels by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which provides vessel identification but has known vulnerabilities, and space-based radio frequency observations, which are independent but lack identification information. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model to probabilistically align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories, accounting for temporal and spatial noise as well as timing discrepancies. The model was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines, and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full model against a null model substantially improved both precision and the ability to detect vessels that have disabled their AIS transponders, reducing several bias issues though a tendency to favor candidates farther from the radio frequency detection remained. Despite these improvements, a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without any model fitting still outperformed the Pair Hidden Markov Model, indicating that the proposed formulation approaches but does not yet surpass simpler heuristic methods for this single-detection scenario.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: This paper investigated how to make brain-to-text decoding systems faster, more portable, and practical for real-world use in people with speech-related neurological conditions. The researchers developed FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end framework that repurposes automatic speech recognition model architectures to decode neural activity recorded from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis into text, replacing the computationally heavy language modeling approaches used in prior systems. The framework was evaluated on publicly available data from a neuroprosthesis user and demonstrated competitive word error rates while running efficiently on a commercially available mobile device with dramatically faster-than-real-time throughput, representing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on mobile hardware. The system also includes mechanisms for adapting to neural signal changes over time and uses gradient-based saliency maps to identify which neural features drive decoding, with these features aligning with established physiological knowledge. Overall, the work addresses key infrastructural barriers to deploying speech neuroprostheses outside of laboratory settings.
items.citation: Jonathan D. McCart, Pranav I. Deevi, Mehdi Azabou et al.. FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.summary: This paper investigates whether open-weight reasoning models can be trained to control real robots through reinforcement learning conducted entirely in simulation, without requiring human demonstrations. The authors developed a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics and applied robot-use reinforcement learning to train a large open-weight model on simulated manipulation tasks, where the model observes the environment, reasons via chain of thought, and directly outputs end-effector poses. Training on simulated benchmarks produced dramatic improvements in task success rates and, critically, the learned skills transferred to an unseen real dual-arm robot and to novel instructions not encountered during training. The trained model proved substantially more robust to task variations than a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, succeeding on novel tasks in familiar scenes at a far higher rate. Importantly, the robotics training did not degrade the model's general capabilities across a range of reasoning, coding, and vision benchmarks, suggesting that robot-use reinforcement learning is a viable component of broad foundation-model post-training.
items.citation: Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo et al.. Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
items.summary: This paper resolves the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas, which relates the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of a twisted character variety for the general linear group to the cohomology of a quiver variety associated to a specific quiver with one vertex and multiple loops. The proof proceeds by transferring the conjecture, via the previously established P=W theorem, into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of a stack of Higgs bundles on a curve. The authors then deploy the theory of BPS Lie algebras together with several recent results—including chi-independence, a stack version of P=C, and an analytic neighborhood theorem—to reduce the problem to a comparison between BPS Lie algebras associated to Higgs bundle stacks and to representation stacks of a preprojective algebra. This final comparison is achieved through a quiver analogue of Markman's tautological generation theorem for BPS Lie algebras. As a consequence, the work yields an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of the character variety in terms of Kac polynomials.
items.citation: Olivier Schiffmann, Eric Vasserot. On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
items.summary: The paper studies the problem of detecting slope changes in multidimensional time series by fitting continuous piecewise-linear functions that share a single breakpoint, examining both a dense setting where any dimension may change slope and a sparse setting where at most a fixed number of dimensions may do so. Despite the resulting optimization problems being nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear programs that can even yield irrational solutions for rational inputs, the authors prove that all six problem variants across three common loss functions are exactly solvable in polynomial time. They developed efficient algorithms for the least-squares case and implemented them, testing on simulated data as well as real-world datasets spanning climate, motion tracking, and engine sensor domains. The dense algorithm handles very large instances in well under a second on a laptop, and both algorithms are orders of magnitude faster than a leading commercial solver, which frequently fails to reach near-optimal solutions within generous time limits on larger instances. These results resolve a seemingly hard class of optimization problems and provide practical tools for scalable changepoint detection in high-dimensional settings.
items.citation: Apoorva Narula, Santanu S. Dey. Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately modeling friction in continuum robots interacting with their environments, where existing approaches inadequately capture static friction and motion hysteresis. The authors developed a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints within the Coulomb friction framework, formulated as a Linear Complementarity Problem. The model accounts for both static and sliding friction, hysteresis behavior, and the robot deformation resulting from environmental contact, while remaining computationally efficient enough for real-time implementation. Experimental validation with a tendon-driven continuum robot demonstrated a substantial reduction in tip position error compared to a frictionless model, confirming the practical utility of the approach for motion planning and control applications.
items.citation: Jia Shen, Junhyoung Ha, Yue Chen. Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
items.summary: This paper introduced TIMBER, a non-CRISPR nucleic acid diagnostic platform that uses repair endonucleases to achieve sequence-specific cleavage of probes containing abasic sites when hybridized to a matched target sequence. Unlike CRISPR-based diagnostics, TIMBER avoids nonspecific collateral nuclease activity, which simplifies multiplexing and integration with amplification methods. The platform achieves single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination and can detect targets at very low concentrations without preamplification, or at the single-copy-per-microliter level when paired with RT-PCR or RT-LAMP, with results readable by fluorescence or lateral flow. The authors validated the approach by detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and demonstrated simultaneous detection of four targets including EGFR mutations relevant to lung cancer genotyping. Overall, TIMBER is presented as a flexible, low-instrumentation diagnostic solution applicable to both infectious disease surveillance and precision oncology.
items.citation: Garden PM, Li Y, Murugan V et al.. Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the potential of human saliva as a noninvasive diagnostic biofluid capable of replacing or supplementing conventional blood-based testing. The authors surveyed salivary biomarkers across a broad range of clinical domains, including metabolic disease, cardiovascular risk, sepsis, endocrinology, infectious diseases, cancer liquid biopsy, and neurodegenerative conditions, while also evaluating the analytical technologies used to detect them, from immunoassays and mass spectrometry to wearable electrochemical biosensors. Existing regulatory-cleared platforms were distinguished from investigational discovery-phase panels to clarify the current state of clinical readiness. Despite substantial promise, the review identifies persistent barriers to mainstream adoption, including unstandardized collection protocols, interference from the oral matrix, and the absence of validated normative reference intervals. The authors conclude that broad clinical translation will require universal sampling standardization, matrix-matched biosensor engineering for ultra-low-concentration detection, and rigorous multicenter prospective trials to establish clinical cutoffs and validate the kinetic relationship between blood and salivary analyte concentrations.
items.citation: Mondal S, Das Sharma A, Mandal SK et al.. Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.. Expert review of molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether dried blood spot or dried saliva spot specimens perform better for universal newborn screening of congenital cytomegalovirus infection. Using a prospective paired-sample pilot across multiple birthing centers, researchers collected both specimen types from tens of thousands of newborns and tested them with quantitative PCR assays, with positive screens confirmed by urine testing. Dried saliva spots did not significantly improve sensitivity for detecting congenital cytomegalovirus compared to dried blood spots, while producing a substantially higher false positive rate. Additionally, dried saliva spot screening frequently exceeded the timeframes required to offer confirmatory diagnostic testing within the critical early window of life. Based on this performance profile, the authors concluded that dried saliva spots do not support population-wide implementation in their newborn screening program.
items.citation: Santander E, Reuvers E, Lacaria M et al.. Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.. International journal of neonatal screening. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing the mouth with a Vitamin D₃ solution could affect the accuracy of saliva-based rapid antigen tests for SARS-CoV-2. Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with samples analyzed by both rapid antigen test and rapid RT-PCR under blinded conditions. The rinse converted a large majority of antigen-positive samples to antigen-negative, substantially reducing overall antigen test positivity, while RT-PCR positivity and viral RNA levels remained largely unchanged. This discordance between antigen and molecular results indicates that the viral RNA was still present in saliva after rinsing, suggesting the rinse interfered with antigen detection rather than eliminating the virus. The findings identify Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing as a previously unrecognized pre-analytical variable that can produce false-negative results in saliva-based rapid antigen testing, with potential implications for public health surveillance and infectious disease screening protocols.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics
items.summary: The paper addressed the need for automated, decentralized diagnostic tools capable of handling infectious disease outbreaks without relying on centralized laboratories. The researchers developed a fully automated centrifugal microfluidic platform that integrates loop-mediated isothermal amplification with computer-vision-based optical readout, requiring only a single button press to execute the complete sample-to-answer workflow. The system was validated for SARS-CoV-2 detection using RNA fragments spiked into water and artificial saliva, achieving consistent detection at low copy numbers per reaction while processing dozens of samples within under an hour. The platform requires no user intervention during operation and is designed to be broadly adaptable to other infectious disease targets, positioning it as a template for rapid molecular diagnostics in resource-limited or point-of-care settings.
items.citation: Akhtar AS, Lapins N, Moura JM et al.. Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, non-sputum alternatives for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, the researchers collected paired saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples from participants with culture-confirmed tuberculosis and matched culture-negative controls, then tested these samples using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity against sputum culture, surpassing the World Health Organization's target sensitivity threshold for a non-sputum diagnostic test, while oral swabs showed high specificity but meaningfully lower sensitivity than saliva. Saliva sensitivity significantly exceeded that of oral swabs, though the two specimen types did not differ significantly in specificity. Both collection methods were well accepted by participants, supporting their potential as practical, low-complexity alternatives to sputum-based tuberculosis diagnosis.

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary:
The abstract describes an active outbreak investigation rather than a completed study with findings, but enough detail is present for a brief summary.

This report describes a multi-country investigation into an outbreak of Andes orthohantavirus linked to an expedition cruise ship operating internationally. Cases arose among both passengers and crew members representing dozens of nationalities, resulting in a notable case fatality proportion. The response required medical evacuation, repatriation, international contact tracing, and coordinated isolation and quarantine measures across multiple jurisdictions. Investigations were ongoing at the time of reporting, with the source of the outbreak, associated risk factors, and routes of transmission not yet fully determined.
