items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future trajectory of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, addressing the need to move beyond centralized laboratory testing toward decentralized, rapid, and accessible approaches. The authors synthesize clinical requirements, technological advances, and translational considerations through case studies drawn from oncology settings including hospitals, outpatient clinics, and dental practices. Key technologies evaluated include microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, smartphone-integrated devices, and advances in nucleic acid and protein biomarker detection alongside imaging modalities. The review also analyzes funding landscapes, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the transition of these technologies from research into commercial use. The authors conclude that interdisciplinary innovation, equitable access, and integration with precision medicine will be central to realizing the potential of point-of-care diagnostics for cancer detection, therapy selection, and treatment monitoring.
items.citation: Seemesh Bhaskar, Saurabh Umrao, Hankeun Lee et al.. Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious syndromes, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, in the context of a rapidly changing global environment. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance to provide a comprehensive overview of the field. A central focus is placed on how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation alter rodent reservoir dynamics and increase the risk of spillover to humans, while also highlighting significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where the burden may be underestimated. The review discusses recent advances including molecular and genomic diagnostics, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems as tools for improved outbreak response. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and enhancing preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring
items.summary: This mega-review examines the current state of wearable sensor technologies for health monitoring, bringing together leading researchers to synthesize advances across the field. The authors cover chemical and biological sensors applied to multiple biofluids such as sweat, saliva, tears, interstitial fluid, and cerebrospinal fluid, alongside physical sensors measuring parameters including heart rate, blood pressure, and body temperature. Device formats reviewed range from smart contact lenses and textiles to mouthguards, wristbands, and implantable systems, with attention to soft electronics, materials science, and energy harvesting strategies that enable practical wearability. The review further addresses signal acquisition and transmission, and the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning to manage the large data volumes generated and enhance analytical performance. The authors conclude by identifying promising research directions and discussing the business, regulatory, and ethical considerations that must be navigated to translate these technologies into clinical and consumer health applications.
items.citation: Laís Canniatti Brazaca, Alvaro Moreno Lozano, Beatriz Mayol et al.. Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces. 2026

items.title: Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics
items.summary: This review paper examines the integration of microfluidic technologies with biosensor platforms and their applications across biomedical and environmental fields. The authors survey a broad range of microfluidic approaches, including inertial separation, acoustofluidics, dielectrophoresis, optofluidics, and immunoassays, alongside biosensor modalities encompassing electrochemical, electrophysiological, plasmonic, Raman, and quantum sensing. These integrated systems are capable of detecting analytes spanning a wide size range, from nanometer-scale molecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins to micrometer-scale exosomes and cells and even small organisms. The review identifies key advantages of such integrated platforms, including enhanced sensitivity, speed, portability, and real-time monitoring, with applications in human and animal health diagnostics, environmental sensing, and point-of-care testing. The authors also address existing technical challenges, future development opportunities, and highlight commercially successful products that have emerged from these integrated microfluidic technologies.
items.citation: Ty Downing Naquin, Chloe M. Naquin, Qian WU et al.. Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus (ANDV), a zoonotic RNA virus transmitted through inhalation of aerosols from infected rodent excreta, is unique among hantaviruses in its capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets and close contact. This paper reviews the clinical, epidemiological, and public health features of ANDV infection to update general physicians on its presentation and management. The most severe manifestation is Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, characterized by acute respiratory failure, haemodynamic instability, organ involvement, and dysregulated immune responses, with disease severity linked to specific haematological and biochemical markers. No approved antiviral treatment or vaccine exists, leaving supportive care as the only management strategy, and case fatality rates remain high. A recent cruise ship outbreak involving passengers of multiple nationalities illustrates how ANDV's combination of human-to-human transmissibility and international travel can rapidly give a regionally endemic pathogen global reach, highlighting the need for clinician awareness and coordinated outbreak preparedness.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of monitoring maritime activities by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which identifies vessels but has known vulnerabilities including spoofing, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full model against a null model substantially improved precision and the ability to detect "dark" vessels that appear in radio frequency data but not in AIS. Despite these improvements, a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without any model fitting remained superior, indicating that the single-detection Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation approaches but does not surpass a well-designed heuristic comparator.

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of deploying speech neuroprostheses — systems that decode neural activity into text for people who have lost the ability to speak — in practical, real-world settings. items.summary: This paper investigates whether open-weight reasoning models can be trained to control real robots through reinforcement learning conducted entirely in simulation, without requiring human demonstrations. The trained model observes its environment, reasons through a chain of thought, and directly outputs end-effector poses without additional scaffolding. items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to gravitational dynamics beyond the standard model. Using a non-parametric joint reconstruction approach, the authors simultaneously infer the effective dark energy density and two gravitational response functions from a combination of CMB, baryon acoustic oscillation, supernova, and large-scale structure datasets. They find a persistent feature in the dark energy density at intermediate redshifts consistent with a phantom divide crossing, a result that proves robust across different data combinations and when gravitational modifications are allowed to vary freely. The gravitational response functions show suggestive enhancements over a similar redshift range, though these are less statistically significant, and including large-scale structure data instead favors a suppressed lensing response. The authors conclude that current departures from the standard cosmological model are most compelling in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravity remain possible but await confirmation from future surveys.

items.title: Antimicrobial-laden PerOssal beads display in vitro inhibition and killing of extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria associated with conflict wounds in Ukraine
items.summary: This study investigated the use of antimicrobial-laden PerOssal hydroxyapatite and calcium sulphate beads as a local drug delivery strategy against extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria isolated from conflict wounds in Ukraine. The researchers tested these beads, loaded with various antimicrobials including gentamicin, tobramycin, cefazolin, rifampicin, and co-amoxiclav, using zone-of-inhibition testing and time-kill analysis against bacterial isolates that were resistant to multiple standard systemic antimicrobials. Single antimicrobial agents such as gentamicin, tobramycin, or cefazolin alone showed only weak growth inhibition, whereas gentamicin combined with rifampicin achieved consistent broad-spectrum bacterial inhibition and killing, and co-amoxiclav-loaded beads inhibited all tested strains. The findings suggest that local delivery of antimicrobials via these beads can achieve sufficient drug concentrations to overcome resistance that would render systemic therapy ineffective. The authors propose that this approach could reduce infection risk in heavily contaminated open fractures when surgical wound excision is delayed, with relevance to both conflict and civilian disaster scenarios, though in vivo validation is still needed.

items.title: Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk
items.summary: This study developed and validated a rapid molecular detection platform for *Streptococcus agalactiae*, the primary causative agent of contagious bovine mastitis, in dairy milk samples. The researchers designed a dual-readout system combining recombinase polymerase amplification with *Pyrococcus furiosus* Argonaute protein activity, targeting the conserved *cfb* gene, with results readable either by real-time fluorescence or lateral flow dipstick formats. The platform was optimized through systematic screening of primer and guide DNA combinations, achieving a detection limit as low as ten copies per microliter with high analytical specificity and no cross-reactivity against non-target bacteria. Field validation using bovine milk samples from multiple dairy farming regions demonstrated complete concordance between both readout formats and a standardized quantitative PCR assay, while all molecular methods outperformed conventional bacteriological culture in identifying positive cases. The authors conclude that this dual-readout platform offers a rapid, reliable, and fieldable diagnostic tool for detecting *S. agalactiae* in bovine milk, with potential utility in dairy herd surveillance and management.
items.citation: Xujie Zhao, Yuying Du, Qianlei Zhu et al.. Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk. Veterinary Sciences. 2026

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines represent an updated clinical practice document developed by the European Society for Vascular Surgery to assist clinicians and patients in managing vascular graft and endograft infections, succeeding a prior version. The recommendations were formulated by synthesizing and evaluating the best available scientific evidence, supplemented by expert opinion, with each recommendation graded by both strength and level of evidence. The guidelines span key topics including definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, management of intracavity and extracavity infections, and follow-up care. A dedicated chapter addresses shared decision-making to support patient involvement, and a further chapter identifies unresolved issues in the field. The resulting set of recommendations aims to provide comprehensive, current guidance on this complex and high-stakes clinical condition.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health
items.summary: This review examined how gut microbial metabolism shapes the biological effects of dietary polyphenols, focusing on the concept that individuals differ meaningfully in their capacity to convert polyphenols into bioactive metabolites. Because many polyphenols are poorly absorbed in the upper gut and reach the colon largely intact, intestinal microorganisms transform them into smaller compounds such as urolithins, equol, and enterolignans, which may have distinct biological activities compared to their parent molecules. The review catalogued major microbial metabotypes—classifications of individuals based on which of these metabolites they produce—and assessed the evidence linking them to health-relevant processes including mitochondrial function, inflammation, endothelial homeostasis, and gut-brain communication, carefully distinguishing human evidence from preclinical findings. The authors concluded that while metabotype-based stratification holds promise for improving the design of nutritional studies and identifying responders, clinical translation is currently hampered by inconsistent methodology, non-standardized analytical thresholds, and insufficient long-term intervention data. Microbial metabotypes are therefore characterized as valuable research and trial-design tools rather than established instruments for personalized dietary prescription.
items.citation: Pasquale Perrone, Stefania D’Angelo. Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health. Nutrients. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from the European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation addressing infection-related risks in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The guidelines were developed in response to the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies used to treat Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics that carry distinct infection risk profiles compared to older agents. The authors synthesized current evidence on risk stratification and the prevention, diagnosis, and management of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections in this immunocompromised population. The update places particular emphasis on preventative strategies tailored to the contemporary treatment landscape, recognizing that potent immune modulation increases susceptibility to opportunistic infections that can cause significant morbidity or mortality. The guidelines supersede prior iterations and are intended to provide clinicians with structured, evidence-based guidance reflecting the most recent developments in both therapeutics and vaccination strategies for inflammatory bowel disease.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of monitoring maritime activities by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which identifies vessels but has known vulnerabilities including spoofing and deliberate deactivation, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model framework to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories by jointly modeling temporal and spatial information alongside noise and timing discrepancies. The approach was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines, and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full model against a null model without match transitions substantially improved both precision and the ability to detect vessels operating without AIS, and largely removed biases toward stationary trajectories. However, the best Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation still did not surpass a simple time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline, indicating that this hand-designed single-detection approach approaches but does not yet exceed straightforward geometric methods.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of deploying brain-to-text speech neuroprostheses in real-world settings, where existing systems rely on computationally intensive language models that produce variable latencies and are impractical outside laboratory environments. The researchers developed FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end framework that adapts automatic speech recognition architectures to decode neural activity from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis into text, while incorporating mechanisms to handle neural signal drift over time. When evaluated on publicly available data from a neuroprosthesis user, the system achieved word error rates as low as approximately four percent and demonstrated successful fine-tuning to maintain performance across future recording sessions. Critically, the framework was shown to run on a commercially available mobile device at speeds far exceeding real-time, representing the first demonstration of mobile brain-to-text decoding. The approach also provided interpretability through gradient-based saliency maps that highlighted neural features consistent with established physiological knowledge, suggesting the models capture meaningful neural representations of speech.
items.citation: Jonathan D. McCart, Pranav I. Deevi, Mehdi Azabou et al.. FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to gravitational dynamics beyond the standard model. Using a non-parametric joint reconstruction approach, the authors simultaneously inferred the effective dark energy density and two gravitational response functions from a combination of CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, supernova, and large-scale structure datasets, with and without a theory-motivated prior from stable Horndeski scalar-tensor models. A persistent feature in the dark energy density around intermediate redshifts was found, corresponding to a crossing of the phantom divide, and this feature proved robust across different data combinations and when gravitational modifications were allowed. The gravitational response functions showed suggestive but less significant enhancements over a similar redshift range, though including large-scale structure data instead favored a suppressed lensing response. The authors conclude that current departures from the standard cosmological model are most clearly manifested in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics remain plausible but await confirmation from future surveys.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the apparent dynamical evolution of dark energy inferred from recent observations is accompanied by corresponding modifications to gravitational dynamics governing clustering and lensing. Using a non-parametric, joint reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to cosmic expansion and the gravitational response functions, without assuming model-specific relationships between these sectors, the authors combine cosmic microwave background data, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, supernova observations, and large-scale structure surveys. They find a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density at intermediate redshift, alongside suggestive low-redshift enhancements in the gravitational responses relative to general relativity predictions that are approximately coincident with this background feature. A covariance-mode analysis reveals that the leading observational constraints are dominated by the background expansion history, while the gravitational sector remains comparatively underconstrained. The authors conclude that current data cannot yet establish whether the features seen in the expansion and gravitational sectors share a common physical origin, leaving this determination to future Stage-IV surveys.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
items.summary: This paper investigates conditions under which braided monoidal infinity-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators, arising from three-dimensional topological quantum field theories, are invertible in the higher Morita category, which would make them determine invertible four-dimensional anomaly theories. The authors examine several classes of derived examples, showing that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves is invertible only when the underlying space is a point, and that convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial when the stack satisfies appropriate descent conditions. A key finding is that non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting, in contrast to the finite braided tensor category case: a specific category of two-shifted D-modules associated to an odd vector space is three-dualizable and non-degenerate yet fails to be factorizable or cofactorizable, with connections to linear Rozansky–Witten theory. The authors also introduce a notion of anomaly for group actions on invertible braided monoidal infinity-categories as a Witt class, and demonstrate that representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity are invertible relative to the quantum Frobenius.
items.citation: Claudia Scheimbauer, Jackson Van Dyke. Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators. arXiv. 2026

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: This paper investigates the emerging capability of large language models to operate directly on the weight parameters of neural networks, a paradigm called Weight-Space Programming, wherein models can interpret, repair, or generate network weights without gradient-based training. To evaluate this capability systematically, the authors developed a benchmark comprising dozens of tasks organized into five tracks covering weight reading, fixing, writing, recognizing impossible edits, and data-free compression, tested across networks ranging from very small control policies to multi-billion parameter language models. Experiments revealed that frontier models can already interpret small networks and write functional control policies from scratch, but consistently fail at patching large language models, compressing networks without access to data, and distinguishing genuinely impossible edits from merely difficult ones. Performance varied substantially across model families, with the strongest tested agents achieving scores roughly around half the maximum on all tasks combined, indicating meaningful but incomplete mastery of this paradigm. The benchmark, task registry, and leaderboard are released publicly to support continued evaluation of this nascent capability.
items.citation: Aayush Marasini, Barsat Khadka, Nick Rahimi. WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.
items.summary: This study investigated the diagnostic utility of adenosine deaminase levels measured in cerebrospinal fluid across a range of central nervous system infections, with particular attention to tropical diseases and HIV-infected patients, populations in which this marker had been insufficiently studied. Researchers analyzed cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase levels alongside other laboratory parameters in over two hundred patients with various microbiologically confirmed diagnoses, comparing them against a non-infectious control group and defining diagnostic cutoff values. Elevated cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase levels were found specifically in tuberculous meningitis and meningococcal meningitis, with the tuberculous group showing the highest levels compared to all other infectious etiologies. The marker demonstrated modest sensitivity and specificity for tuberculous meningitis, with higher cutoff values identified in the setting of central nervous system coinfections, and levels correlated positively with cerebrospinal fluid protein and weakly negatively with cerebrospinal fluid glucose. The authors conclude that cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase may serve as a supportive, though not standalone, diagnostic tool in suspected tuberculous meningitis, meningococcal meningitis, and central nervous system coinfections.
items.citation: Farias LABG, Neto OMV, Sobrinho EPL et al.. Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.. Arquivos de neuro-psiquiatria. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether the FilmArray BCID2 multiplex PCR panel, designed for blood culture identification, could be applied off-label to excised heart valve tissue from patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis. Researchers compared BCID2 results against both blood cultures and conventional valve cultures from a surgical cohort. When benchmarked against blood cultures, the assay showed moderate sensitivity and a high positive predictive value, but poor specificity and a low negative predictive value, with overall agreement between methods being weak. Against conventional valve culture as the reference, specificity was perfect but sensitivity was very low. The authors conclude that while the BCID2 panel may serve as a complementary diagnostic tool in selected patients, a negative result cannot exclude infective endocarditis, and larger multicentre studies are needed to clarify its clinical utility.
items.citation: Bilewska A, Skrzeczyńska J, Dorota M et al.. Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Rapid identification of porcine bacterial pathogens using an artificial intelligence Raman microbial analyzer for biology.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether an artificial intelligence-driven Raman spectroscopy platform could rapidly and accurately identify bacterial pathogens isolated from diseased pigs in a clinical veterinary diagnostic setting. Bacterial isolates were collected from diseased pig tissues, with species-level identity confirmed by polymerase chain reaction before Raman spectral data were acquired, providing reliable reference labels for assessing system performance. The commercial system, which combines Raman spectroscopy with deep learning, was tested against fourteen clinically relevant swine bacterial pathogens and delivered identification results in approximately two minutes per isolate. The system achieved perfect recall for some of the most common species tested and high recall exceeding ninety percent for several other important pathogens. The authors conclude that this approach offers a rapid, label-free, and highly automated alternative to conventional culture-based and molecular methods, with practical value for timely decision-making in routine veterinary diagnostics and potential relevance to public health given the zoonotic nature of some swine pathogens.
items.citation: Lu C-H, Ke N-J, Liu C-C et al.. Rapid identification of porcine bacterial pathogens using an artificial intelligence Raman microbial analyzer for biology.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular diagnostic method for detecting Group B Streptococcus, a major cause of neonatal infections, using a bacteriophage lysin to lyse bacterial cells and release nucleic acids for real-time PCR detection. The approach targeted the GBS cylA gene and a human internal control gene, achieving complete lysis and nucleic acid extraction within five minutes and total turnaround in approximately thirty-five minutes, compared to the eighteen to forty-eight hours required for conventional culture. The assay demonstrated no cross-reactivity and achieved high sensitivity and specificity in a clinical cohort of vaginal swab samples, with specificity further improving after sequencing-based resolution of discordant results. In a second validation cohort, the assay markedly outperformed antigen-based testing in sensitivity. The authors conclude that this bacteriophage lysin-based rapid PCR method shows strong diagnostic performance and potential utility for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, pending further real-world validation.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated non-pharmaceutical interventions affected rates of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children over time. Using a large retrospective cohort of pediatric patients presenting with suspected acute tonsillopharyngitis at a tertiary outpatient clinic, researchers compared Group A Streptococcus positivity rates across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods spanning roughly seven years. Positivity rates rose progressively across all three periods, with the lowest rates seen before the pandemic and the highest in the post-pandemic period, a trend that persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and diagnostic method. Older age and male sex were also independently associated with a greater likelihood of testing positive. The authors conclude that these trends likely reflect a combination of shifting healthcare utilization patterns, diagnostic practices, age distributions, and transmission dynamics, and call for continued surveillance to better characterize pediatric Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Epidemiological surveillance reveals major pathogen dynamics in Brazilian Nile tilapia aquaculture from 2023 to 2025.
items.summary: This study investigated the major pathogen dynamics threatening Nile tilapia aquaculture across Brazil's three primary producing regions over a two-year surveillance period. Researchers analyzed tens of thousands of diagnostic samples using bacteriological methods, real-time PCR, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, applying generalized linear models, time-series analysis, co-detection network analysis, and pharmacological modeling to characterize pathogen occurrence and behavior. The surveillance revealed that the disease landscape is broader than previously recognized, with Infectious Spleen and Kidney Necrosis Virus, *Lactococcus* spp., *Flavobacterium* spp., and *Streptococcus* spp. all representing major concerns rather than streptococcosis alone. Most pathogens displayed stationary, endemic dynamics, while *Streptococcus* spp. showed non-stationary patterns consistent with active geographic expansion into the Northeast region, and antimicrobial resistance was structured by both pathogen identity and antibiotic, with fry exhibiting higher minimum inhibitory concentrations. The authors conclude that these findings provide a data-driven baseline to support regionalized early-warning systems and more rational antimicrobial stewardship in Brazilian tilapia production.
items.citation: Cardoso-Guimarães M, Fernandez-Alarcon MF, Correa R et al.. Epidemiological surveillance reveals major pathogen dynamics in Brazilian Nile tilapia aquaculture from 2023 to 2025.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviewed advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing the evidence base that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for tuberculosis detection and drug-resistance testing. The review covers progress across screening, diagnosis, and treatment-monitoring tools, encompassing digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection, decentralised molecular platforms including low-complexity nucleic acid amplification tests, and expanded use of non-sputum specimens to improve diagnosis in children and sputum-scarce populations. Drug-resistance testing has advanced through rapid molecular assays and targeted next-generation sequencing, while urine-based lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic gains specifically in people with HIV and advanced disease. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarkers show promise for prognosis and triage, yet no biomarker has yet met WHO criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that despite meaningful progress, substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain, underscoring ongoing research and programmatic priorities.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examined point-of-care testing as a diagnostic approach for infectious diseases, motivated by the growing global burden of such diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the core technical platforms underlying current point-of-care technologies, including lateral flow assays, chemiluminescence immunoassays, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and microfluidic chip systems, alongside their application across a range of clinical infection types spanning respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, urinary, and sexually transmitted infections. The review also addressed existing limitations of these technologies, including constraints in detection sensitivity, quality control, cost, and integration into clinical workflows. The authors argue that ongoing advances in nanomaterials, microfluidic engineering, artificial intelligence, and industry standardization are driving improvements in performance and systematic deployment. Based on this trajectory, the review concludes that point-of-care testing holds strong potential to become a central diagnostic tool in both precision clinical care and broader public health efforts to control infectious disease outbreaks.
items.citation: Fang Q, Lin Y, Hu G et al.. Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives

items.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
items.summary: This paper developed a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to extract cell-free nucleic acids from plasma without requiring any external power source or laboratory pipetting equipment. The device integrates manually operated valves, a pump, and onboard reagent storage to perform a complete extraction workflow—including lysis, binding, washing, and elution—in roughly half an hour. Performance was benchmarked against both manual benchtop and automated robotic extraction methods, with the device achieving DNA recoveries comparable to the commercial bench protocol in spiked aqueous samples, and notably higher recoveries from small volumes of human plasma. Clinical utility was demonstrated using patient samples infected with cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, and chikungunya virus, where quantitative PCR amplification results closely matched those from standard protocols. The authors conclude that this instrument-free extraction tool could serve as a practical bridge between existing nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralized diagnostics in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Musaddaq G, Ehsan L, Yoga Y et al.. Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies used to detect and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The paper covers two primary approaches: nucleic acid amplification methods, including polymerase chain reaction variants and isothermal amplification techniques, and pathogen characterization through next-generation sequencing. Advances in polymerase chain reaction focus on improving speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care applicability, while isothermal amplification methods offer simplified temperature requirements that make them particularly suited to decentralized testing settings. CRISPR-based detection systems are highlighted as an emerging complement to amplification methods, and next-generation sequencing is described as enabling the identification of novel pathogens, outbreak tracking, transmission monitoring, and microbiome analysis relevant to disease susceptibility. The authors conclude that future progress in infectious disease molecular diagnostics will come from integrating multiple technologies into hybrid platforms that address the current limitations of individual approaches.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.
items.summary: The paper investigated the development of a portable device for nucleic acid-based infectious disease testing, aiming to overcome the size limitations of conventional diagnostic instruments that restrict their use in field settings. The researchers created the QMini by simplifying its fluidic module through direct pump-to-reaction-chamber connections and protecting its optical module from ambient light using a three-dimensional-printed enclosure. They applied the device to detect synthetic nucleic acid sequences from respiratory syncytial virus B, SARS-CoV-2, and influenza A using a bead-based assay with quantum dot barcodes. The QMini successfully detected low copy numbers of each target pathogen while showing minimal cross-reactivity against several nontarget viral nucleic acid sequences. The authors conclude that this miniaturized platform advances the portability of quantum dot barcode-based nucleic acid testing for potential use in decentralized infectious disease diagnostics.
items.citation: Mahbub N, Osborne M, Chen H et al.. QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.. ACS nanoscience Au. 2026

items.title: Gut microbiota dynamics in free-range layer hens during outbreaks of spotty liver disease and fowl cholera—a field study
items.summary: This field study examined how gut microbiota dynamics, hen performance, and disease progression unfolded in a commercial free-range layer flock experiencing concurrent outbreaks of spotty liver disease and fowl cholera. Because such complex, multi-pathogen outbreak scenarios cannot be ethically or practically reproduced under controlled laboratory conditions, the researchers conducted observations directly on farm, tracking weekly performance metrics and microbial community composition across major gut sections. One group of hens received a precision biotic consisting of a synthetic glycan product, while a control group did not, allowing descriptive comparison of outcomes between the two. Supplemented birds showed associations with both higher egg output and higher cumulative mortality, alongside differences in intestinal microbial community composition and liver congestion compared to controls, though the unreplicated design limits causal interpretation. The study offers rare real-world observations of concurrent disease outbreaks in a production setting, providing ecological and microbial data intended to inform the design of future controlled investigations into disease dynamics and biotic interventions in poultry.
items.citation: Friedrich Petranyi, Maria M. Whitton, Edina Lobo et al.. Gut microbiota dynamics in free-range layer hens during outbreaks of spotty liver disease and fowl cholera—a field study. Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize information across multiple omics layers — including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics — and assess how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful biological patterns from these complex, high-dimensional datasets. The review covers the application of this combined approach across the drug development pipeline, encompassing target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas including oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate how these technologies converge to enable more precise therapeutic interventions. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence marks a transformative new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with a focus on how their acellular nature creates classification ambiguities across different jurisdictions. The authors analyze how major regulatory frameworks, including those of the European Union, the United States, and other regions, apply existing medicinal product categories to extracellular vesicle-based products in inconsistent ways, generating challenges around quality assessment, potency strategies, comparability, and cross-regional clinical development. A key focus is the European guidance clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal products definition, contrasting with the approach of treating such products as drugs and biologics subject to premarket review elsewhere. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products can and should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks, provided regulatory tools are applied consistently and outstanding grey zones in classification criteria and quality attributes are resolved through ongoing dialogue. Rather than proposing new normative frameworks, the review synthesizes the current state of regulatory and technical considerations to support harmonization efforts among international agencies and scientific societies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection

items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, addressing the need for rapid, accurate testing outside centralized laboratory settings. The authors surveyed advances in sample preparation, nucleic acid and protein biomarker detection, and imaging modalities compatible with decentralized deployment across diverse clinical environments. Key enabling technologies evaluated include microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, and smartphone-integrated devices, with attention to their practical limitations. The review also analyzes funding landscapes, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the translation of these technologies from academic research to commercial products. The authors conclude that point-of-care molecular diagnostics hold transformative potential for cancer detection, therapy selection, treatment monitoring, and personalized medicine, provided that interdisciplinary innovation and equitable access are prioritized.
items.citation: Seemesh Bhaskar, Saurabh Umrao, Hankeun Lee et al.. Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigated how convolutional neural networks exploit contextual background information when classifying agricultural images, and whether the internal representations of hidden neurons can be made interpretable using a technique called Concept Induction. The researchers applied this approach across five agricultural datasets with varying degrees of contextual bias, examining four CNN architectures at multiple network depths and patch locations by encoding quantitative image descriptors into a knowledge graph and deriving logical expressions characterizing neuron activations. A substantial portion of neuron-feature pairs were statistically validated, with validation rates being highest at intermediate network depths and most strongly associated with edge, Gabor, and texture features. Notably, stronger contextual bias in a dataset did not correspond to higher neuron-feature validation rates, suggesting that a network's behavioral reliance on background context and the semantic interpretability of its hidden neurons are distinct phenomena. The authors conclude that Concept Induction offers a complementary lens to patch-based bias detection for understanding what CNN hidden layers actually represent.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
items.summary: This paper presents KELP, a Lagrangian particle tracking software designed to follow virtual particles through ocean model velocity fields in order to study transport pathways, connectivity, and dispersion. The tool is specifically built to operate on unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix equal-area grids, including those used by kilometre-scale digital twin ocean models, and is architecturally designed to be operated by coding agents powered by language models. The authors demonstrate that structured documentation and short task instructions called skills substantially improved the ability of language models to correctly prepare and execute Lagrangian studies, with completeness scores rising markedly across multiple tested models. KELP reproduced particle distributions consistent with other established trackers, and trajectories computed on HEALPix grids converged toward those on the native model mesh as grid resolution increased, supporting the use of HEALPix output for ensemble Lagrangian statistics when original mesh data are unavailable. The software demonstrated strong computational performance, handling very large particle ensembles and multi-decadal simulations, with an application to the Beaufort Gyre revealing that transport to Fram Strait occurs over timescales of years to decades.
items.citation: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin et al.. KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection systems, framing the decision on each detected bounding box as a hypothesis test where the null hypothesis assumes the box contains an in-distribution object. The key insight is that the null distribution varies with box size and border contact, so a box should only be compared against in-distribution boxes sharing those same geometric properties, which provides a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate and reveals structure hidden by a single pooled null distribution. The authors also argue that features extracted before class-specific layers better preserve information about unknown objects, since later layers are trained exclusively on in-distribution classes and discard signals that could distinguish novel objects. Based on these principles, they propose PLUM, a training-free scoring method that pools backbone features from the last stage within a box and ranks their distance to in-distribution classes using box-conditional comparisons. PLUM achieves leading detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models, outperforming compared methods on both PASCAL-VOC and BDD100K datasets.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: This paper investigates whether Redshift Space Distortions (RSD) could mimic a parity-violating signal in measurements of the galaxy four-point correlation function (4PCF), which has recently been used to search for cosmological parity violation. The authors analyze the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density to third order in Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory, incorporating biased tracer expansion, tidal bias, wide-angle effects through a local line-of-sight definition, and generalization to arbitrary cosmological backgrounds. By expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, they demonstrate that angular momentum selection rules encoded in Wigner 3-j symbols force all parity-odd contributions from RSD to vanish when averaged over all line-of-sight orientations, in both the plane-parallel and full wide-angle cases. This result holds up to leading order in general relativistic corrections and applies to both the configuration-space 4PCF and its Fourier-space counterpart, the trispectrum. The finding is significant because it supports the interpretation that any observed parity-violation signal in isotropic 4PCF estimators cannot be attributed to a systematic artefact from RSD, lending greater credibility to such detections as potentially physical in origin.
items.citation: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.. Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of antigen-based rapid test kits for six common pediatric respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus—comparing them against a multiplex PCR reference panel. In a prospective paired-specimen design, nasopharyngeal swabs from children presenting with respiratory tract infections were tested in parallel by both methods, with positive specimens subjected to quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Sensitivity varied considerably across viral targets, ranging from low for adenovirus to moderate for human metapneumovirus, while specificity exceeded ninety-nine percent for all six viruses. Critically, antigen test sensitivity was strongly dependent on viral load, approaching ninety to one hundred percent at high viral concentrations but falling below fifty percent at low viral loads, a pattern that was consistent across all six pathogens. The authors conclude that rapid antigen tests reliably identify children carrying the highest viral burdens—those most likely to have acute symptomatic infection—and that viral load is the principal determinant of antigen test performance regardless of the specific respiratory virus being targeted.
items.citation: Kitagawa D, Di Lorenzo A, Okamura T et al.. Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: The study examined whether adding reflex multiplex PCR testing after a negative rapid antigen test improves viral detection in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory infections. In a single-center prospective cohort, children first underwent a five-target rapid antigen test, and those testing negative could then receive multiplex PCR at physician discretion. Rapid antigen testing alone identified only a minority of viral cases, while reflex PCR among antigen-negative children who were tested returned a high proportion of positive results, with rhinovirus/enterovirus—not covered by the antigen panel—being the most commonly identified pathogen. A negative antigen test therefore could not exclude viral infection, and reflex PCR substantially increased diagnostic yield, though selective use of the follow-on test means the reported yield is a lower bound. Antibiotic use was high regardless of whether a virus was detected, and the appropriateness of this prescribing could not be assessed because systematic bacterial testing was not performed.
items.citation: Bedir AZ, Saf C, Yörük MA. Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.. Irish journal of medical science. 2026

items.title: Variant escape site mapping and characterization of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid rapid antigen test antibodies.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples
items.summary: This prospective study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit for detecting respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus in children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with acute respiratory symptoms, using multiplex real-time PCR as the reference standard. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from children aged eighteen years and under, with the rapid antigen test performed at the point of care alongside PCR testing. The rapid test demonstrated very high sensitivity and specificity for both pathogens, with excellent agreement with PCR results for adenovirus and RSV alike. Age-related patterns emerged, with RSV positivity concentrated among infants under one year and adenovirus positivity peaking in school-aged children, while conjunctival injection and fever independently predicted adenovirus infection and cough with young age predicted RSV. The authors conclude that the kit's ability to simultaneously detect both pathogens from a single sample with high accuracy supports its potential utility for timely clinical decision-making in pediatric emergency settings.
items.citation: Ates B, Kacar A, Kok S et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples. 2026
